name: MODEL_GARDEN_MODEL_NAME
description: Identifies a Model Garden model by its publisher, model name and version, in publishers/publisher/models/name@version form, to deploy as a remote model.

name: model_name
description: Name of the model being created or replaced; it must be unique in the dataset, is case-sensitive and follows the naming rules of a BigQuery table.

name: model_option_list
description: List of options that configure a model, starting with MODEL_TYPE and followed by training, data split, tuning, remote model and registry settings.

name: MODEL_PATH
description: Gives the Cloud Storage location of the model to import, which BigQuery reads using the credentials of the user who runs the statement.

name: MODEL_REGISTRY
description: Names the registry the model is registered with when it is created; the only value is VERTEX_AI, the Vertex AI Model Registry.

name: MODEL_TYPE
description: Required option that selects the kind of model to build, for example LINEAR_REG, KMEANS, BOOSTED_TREE_CLASSIFIER or ARIMA_PLUS.

name: NON_SEASONAL_ORDER
description: Gives the non-seasonal p, d and q tuple of an ARIMA_PLUS model; it needs AUTO_ARIMA to be FALSE and cannot be used when forecasting multiple series.

name: NUM_CLUSTERS
description: Sets the number of clusters a k-means model identifies in the input data; it can also take a tuning range or candidates.

name: NUM_FACTORS
description: Sets the number of latent factors a matrix factorization model uses; it can also take a tuning range or candidates.

name: NUM_PARALLEL_TREE
description: Sets how many trees are built in parallel in each boosting iteration; a value above 1 trains a boosted random forest.

name: NUM_PRINCIPAL_COMPONENTS
description: Sets how many principal components a PCA model keeps; it is given instead of PCA_EXPLAINED_VARIANCE_RATIO.

name: NUM_TRIALS
description: Sets the maximum number of submodels trained during hyperparameter tuning, and must be given to turn tuning on.

name: Object tables
description: Read-only tables over unstructured objects in Cloud Storage that expose object metadata, so the objects can be listed, queried and processed with SQL.
notes: ObjectRef functions (OBJ.MAKE_REF, OBJ.FETCH_METADATA, OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL, OBJ.GET_READ_URL) and EXTERNAL_OBJECT_TRANSFORM are missing; only the object_metadata and uris options are accepted (max_staleness, metadata_cache_mode refused); each URI allows one '*' wildcard.

name: ON table(ALL TEXT COLUMNS | column_list)
description: Names the table to index and which columns to cover, either every text column of the table or an explicit list of columns.

name: ON table with FILTER USING (expression)
description: Row access policy clause that names the table and gives the filter expression selecting which rows the policy principals can see.

name: OPTIMIZATION_OBJECTIVE
description: Sets the objective function AutoML optimizes during training, such as MINIMIZE_RMSE for regression or MAXIMIZE_AU_ROC for classification.

name: OPTIMIZE_STRATEGY
description: Chooses the training strategy for linear regression: AUTO_STRATEGY, BATCH_GRADIENT_DESCENT or NORMAL_EQUATION.

name: OPTIMIZER
description: Chooses the optimizer used to train a neural network model, such as ADAM, ADAGRAD, FTRL, RMSPROP or SGD.

name: OPTIONS()
description: Clause that attaches a list of name and value settings to the object being created or altered, such as a table, view, dataset or model.

name: OPTIONS( uris=[...], format='...', ... )
description: Option list of CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE that gives the Cloud Storage source URIs and the data format, plus any other format-specific settings.
notes: Formats other than CSV, NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON, AVRO, ORC and PARQUET (GOOGLE_SHEETS, DATASTORE_BACKUP, DELTA_LAKE, ICEBERG, CLOUD_BIGTABLE) are refused in DDL; options outside the decoded list (for example max_staleness, metadata_cache_mode, file_set_spec_type, reference_file_schema_uri, sheet_range, expiration_timestamp) are refused; only gs:// URIs are accepted.

name: organization_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER ORGANIZATION SET OPTIONS can set, such as the default encryption key, default time zone, query job timeout and default location.

name: Parameters
description: Named inputs declared for a function or stored procedure, each with a name and a data type, and for procedures an optional IN, OUT or INOUT mode.

name: PARTITION BY
description: Clause that divides a table into partitions by a date, timestamp, datetime or integer range column, or by ingestion time, so queries can read fewer partitions.

name: PARTITION BY, CLUSTER BY, OPTIONS(...)
description: Table layout and settings clauses of CREATE TABLE: partitioning by an expression, clustering by up to four columns, and an option list.

name: partition_expression
description: Expression that determines how a table, materialized view or vector index is partitioned, such as a date column, a truncated timestamp or an integer range bucket.

name: PCA_EXPLAINED_VARIANCE_RATIO
description: Sets the share of variance, between 0 and 1, that the kept principal components must explain; it is given instead of NUM_PRINCIPAL_COMPONENTS.

name: PCA_SOLVER
description: Chooses the algorithm that computes the principal components in a PCA model: FULL eigendecomposition, RANDOMIZED PCA or AUTO.

name: Primary key / foreign key constraints (informational, not enforced)
description: Table constraints that declare primary keys and foreign key links between tables; BigQuery records them but does not enforce them when data is written.

name: privacy_policy
description: View option that sets an analysis rule, such as an aggregation threshold policy requiring a minimum number of distinct privacy units behind each result row.

name: procedure_option_list
description: Settings for a stored procedure, such as strict mode checks and description, and for Apache Spark procedures the engine, runtime version and container image.

name: project_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER PROJECT SET OPTIONS can set, such as the default encryption key, time zone, query job timeout, SQL dialect, connection and location.

name: PROMPT_COL
description: Names the column in the tuning data table that holds the prompt for supervised tuning; the default is a column called prompt.

name: PRUNING_METHOD
description: Chooses whether redundant insights are removed from a contribution analysis model: NO_PRUNING or PRUNE_REDUNDANT_INSIGHTS.

name: query_statement
description: The GoogleSQL query whose result provides the training data of a model; its columns become input features, except the label and data split columns.

name: RATING_COL
description: Names the column that holds the rating in the training data of a matrix factorization model.

name: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
description: Manually refreshes a materialized view so that it picks up the latest changes in its base tables, by calling the BQ.REFRESH_MATERIALIZED_VIEW procedure.

name: REMOTE
description: Clause that creates a function or model whose logic runs in an external service reached through a connection, not in code written in the statement.

name: REMOTE_SERVICE_TYPE
description: Picks the Google Cloud AI service a remote model calls, such as Cloud Natural Language, Translation, Vision, Document AI or Speech-to-Text.

name: RESERVATION_AFFINITY_KEY
description: Gives the Compute Engine reservation key, compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name, which is needed when RESERVATION_AFFINITY_TYPE is SPECIFIC_RESERVATION.

name: RESERVATION_AFFINITY_TYPE
description: Chooses whether a deployed open model consumes Compute Engine reservations: NO_RESERVATION, ANY_RESERVATION or one SPECIFIC_RESERVATION.

name: RESERVATION_AFFINITY_VALUES
description: Gives the full resource name of the Compute Engine reservation to use, required when RESERVATION_AFFINITY_TYPE is SPECIFIC_RESERVATION.

name: reservation_option_list
description: Settings of a new slot reservation, such as slot capacity, edition, idle slot use, autoscaling limit, job concurrency, secondary location and labels.

name: RETURNS TABLE <schema>
description: Clause of CREATE TABLE FUNCTION that declares the schema of the returned table as column names and types; if omitted it is inferred from the query.

name: SCALE_FEATURES
description: Controls whether numeric features are scaled to unit variance in a PCA model; they are always centered to a zero mean.

name: schema_option_list
description: Settings for a new dataset, such as default KMS key, default table and partition expiration, description, labels, location and storage billing model.

name: schema_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER SCHEMA SET OPTIONS can change on a dataset, such as default expiration times, encryption key, description, labels and case sensitivity.

name: SEASONALITIES
description: Lists the seasonal patterns, such as daily, weekly or monthly, to model in a time series; the default AUTO infers them from the data.

name: select_list
description: The columns and expressions in a TRANSFORM clause that preprocess query results before training, written like a SELECT list.

name: snapshot_option_list
description: Settings for a new table snapshot, such as expiration time, friendly name, description and labels.

name: SPEECH_RECOGNIZER
description: Names the Speech-to-Text recognizer that a speech remote model uses, in projects/number/locations/location/recognizers/id form; a default recognizer is used if omitted.

name: STANDARDIZE_FEATURES
description: Controls whether numerical features are standardized before a k-means model is trained.

name: SUBSAMPLE
description: Sets the fraction of training rows randomly sampled before growing trees in each boosting iteration, which helps prevent overfitting.

name: Table definition files for external tables
description: JSON definitions of external data, giving source URIs, format and schema, used with the bq tool to create external tables instead of DDL.

name: Table expiration
description: Setting that makes a table delete itself at a given time, through the expiration_timestamp option, or after a default period set on its dataset.

name: table_function_options_list
description: Settings for a table function, namely a description, written in the NAME=VALUE form used by other option lists.

name: table_option_list
description: Settings for a table, such as expiration, partition expiration, partition filter requirement, encryption key, description, labels, change history and maximum staleness.

name: table_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER TABLE SET OPTIONS can change on a table, such as expiration, description, labels, friendly name and partition settings.

name: TF_VERSION
description: Chooses the TensorFlow version, 1.15 or 2.8.0, used to train a DNN model; 2.8.0 uses TensorFlow 2 with the Keras API.

name: TIME_SERIES_DATA_COL
description: Names the column that holds the values to forecast in a time series model, of type INT64, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC or FLOAT64.

name: TIME_SERIES_ID_COL
description: Names one or more ID columns so that a single query can fit and forecast several time series, each ID identifying one series.

name: TIME_SERIES_LENGTH_FRACTION
description: Sets the fraction of the most recent time points used to model the trend component; all points still model the non-trend part.

name: TIME_SERIES_TIMESTAMP_COL
description: Names the column that holds the time points of the training data in a time series model, of type TIMESTAMP, DATE or DATETIME.

name: TOP_K_INSIGHTS_BY_APRIORI_SUPPORT
description: Sets the maximum number of insights, ranked by their apriori_support value, that a contribution analysis model returns; it cannot be used with MIN_APRIORI_SUPPORT.

name: TRANSFORM
description: Clause that lists the feature preprocessing done during model creation and applies it again automatically at prediction and evaluation.
notes: edition:Full edition only (the lite edition answers 400 invalidQuery).|TRANSFORM works for linear/logistic regression, KMEANS, boosted trees, random forests and TRANSFORM_ONLY; * REPLACE, expression.*, named preprocessing arguments and WARM_START are refused.

name: TREE_METHOD
description: Chooses the tree construction algorithm for boosted tree models: AUTO, EXACT, APPROX or HIST.

name: TREND_SMOOTHING_WINDOW_SIZE
description: Sets a center moving-average window that smooths the historical trend component of a time series model, without changing forecasts.

name: TRUNCATE TABLE
description: Removes all rows from a table while leaving its metadata intact, including the schema, description and labels.

name: USER_COL
description: Names the column that holds the user in the training data of a matrix factorization model.

name: VERTEX_AI_MODEL_ID
description: Sets the Vertex AI model ID to register the model under, which needs MODEL_REGISTRY to be VERTEX_AI; the BigQuery ML model name is used if omitted.

name: VERTEX_AI_MODEL_VERSION_ALIASES
description: Sets Vertex AI model aliases to attach when a model is registered, so a version can be referenced without knowing its version ID.

name: view_column_name_list
description: Optional list of column names for a view, which may differ from the names in its query but must match their number.

name: view_column_option_list
description: Settings for a view column, namely its description.

name: view_column_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER COLUMN SET OPTIONS can change on a view column, namely its description.

name: view_option_list
description: Settings for a view, such as expiration time, friendly name, description, labels and a privacy policy.

name: view_set_options_list
description: Options that ALTER VIEW SET OPTIONS can change on a view, such as expiration time, friendly name, description and labels.

name: WALS_ALPHA
description: Adjusts how strongly user feedback affects recommendation confidence in the loss function of IMPLICIT matrix factorization models.

name: WARM_START
description: Retrains an existing model with new data, new options or both, keeping the earlier options unless overridden; iteration numbering restarts at zero.

name: XGBOOST_VERSION
description: Chooses the XGBoost library version used to train a boosted tree model.

name: DELETE
description: Removes rows from a table. A WHERE clause is required, and a condition that is always true deletes every row while keeping the table itself.

name: DELETE FROM
description: The DELETE form that includes the optional FROM keyword before the target table, as in DELETE FROM table_name WHERE condition.
notes: Volatile WHERE predicates (RAND, GENERATE_UUID) are refused; a correlated WHERE subquery that can raise a runtime error is refused (DELETE subqueries require total sources).

name: DELETE ... WHERE
description: The mandatory WHERE condition of a DELETE, evaluated for each row; rows for which it is TRUE are removed and all others are kept.
notes: Volatile WHERE predicates (RAND, GENERATE_UUID) are refused; a correlated WHERE subquery that can raise a runtime error is refused (DELETE subqueries require total sources).

name: DELETE with subquery
description: Deletes rows chosen by a subquery in the WHERE condition, such as products that do not appear in another table; NOT EXISTS can express the same filter.

name: DELETE with WHERE clause
description: Deletes only the rows that match a simple WHERE filter, for example rows whose quantity is 0, and leaves every other row unchanged.

name: EXPORT DATA
description: Runs a query and writes its results to an external destination such as Cloud Storage, Amazon S3, Bigtable, Pub/Sub or Spanner, with options for format and location.

name: INSERT
description: Adds new rows to a table, taking the rows either from literal VALUES lists or from the result of a query.

name: INSERT INTO
description: INSERT with the optional INTO keyword before the target table name, followed by an optional column list and then the rows to add.

name: INSERT INTO ... SELECT
description: Adds every row produced by a SELECT query to the target table, so data can be copied or reshaped from other tables in a single statement.

name: INSERT INTO ... VALUES
description: Adds one or more rows written directly in the statement as parenthesized value lists, one list per row, matched to the listed columns.

name: INSERT SELECT
description: Insert statement whose input is a query, including a query that starts with a WITH clause, used to copy rows from one table into another.

name: INSERT using explicit values
description: Inserts rows from literal values typed into the statement, where the DEFAULT keyword can stand in for a column's default value.

name: INSERT VALUES with subquery
description: Inserts a row in which one of the values is computed by a scalar subquery rather than written as a literal.

name: INSERT with ARRAY types
description: Inserts a row whose column holds an ARRAY, with the value written as an array literal such as a list of numbers in square brackets.

name: INSERT with RANGE types
description: Inserts rows into a column of type RANGE, with each value giving a start and end such as a date range, which queries can then read back.

name: INSERT with STRUCT types
description: Inserts rows into a table with STRUCT columns, supplying each nested record as a struct value whose fields match the column definition.

name: INSERT without column names
description: Inserts values without listing target columns, so each value is matched to a table column by its position in the table definition.

name: LOAD DATA
description: Loads data from external source objects, such as Cloud Storage, into a table; INTO appends rows and OVERWRITE replaces the table contents.

name: load_option_list
description: The list of name=value options in LOAD DATA that describe the source data, such as its format and locations, plus format-specific settings like CSV delimiters.

name: MERGE
description: Combines inserts, updates and deletes in one statement by matching source rows to target rows on a condition and applying the first applicable WHEN clause.

name: MERGE INTO
description: MERGE with the optional INTO keyword before the target table that is changed using the rows of the USING source.
notes: UPDATE and MERGE refuse a target table that has a column named rowid; a correlated WHERE subquery that can raise a runtime error is refused (UPDATE subqueries require total sources); volatile FROM/USING sources and volatile predicates (RAND, GENERATE_UUID) are refused; a statement whose written rows hold a non-finite FLOAT64 value (NaN, +/-inf) is refused.

name: TRUNCATE
description: TRUNCATE TABLE removes every row from a table in one step while keeping the table, its schema, description and labels.

name: UPDATE
description: Changes column values in existing rows of a table that match a WHERE condition, using SET to list the new values.

name: UPDATE ... FROM
description: UPDATE form with a FROM clause that joins the target table to other tables so new values can be computed from their columns; a target row may match at most one source row.
notes: UPDATE and MERGE refuse a target table that has a column named rowid; a correlated WHERE subquery that can raise a runtime error is refused (UPDATE subqueries require total sources); volatile FROM/USING sources and volatile predicates (RAND, GENERATE_UUID) are refused; a statement whose written rows hold a non-finite FLOAT64 value (NaN, +/-inf) is refused.

name: UPDATE nested fields
description: Changes values inside a STRUCT column, either individual fields reached with dot notation or the entire struct replaced at once.

name: UPDATE repeated records
description: Adds or removes entries in a column of repeated records, an ARRAY of STRUCT values, by rebuilding the array with ARRAY subqueries or ARRAY_CONCAT.

name: UPDATE ... SET
description: The SET clause of UPDATE, a comma-separated list of column = expression assignments where the expression may be DEFAULT to restore the column default.
notes: UPDATE and MERGE refuse a target table that has a column named rowid; a correlated WHERE subquery that can raise a runtime error is refused (UPDATE subqueries require total sources); volatile FROM/USING sources and volatile predicates (RAND, GENERATE_UUID) are refused; a statement whose written rows hold a non-finite FLOAT64 value (NaN, +/-inf) is refused.

name: UPDATE statement using join between three tables
description: Updates one table using conditions that span two other tables, with the target's join predicate in WHERE and the extra tables joined using JOIN with ON.

name: UPDATE using joins
description: Updates rows with values taken from another table, written either with a correlated subquery or with a FROM clause that joins the two tables.

name: UPDATE with WHERE clause
description: Changes only the rows that satisfy a WHERE condition, for example lowering quantities for matching products, and can also reset a column to its default.

name: CASE
description: As an expression, returns the result of the first WHEN condition that is TRUE, else the ELSE result or NULL; as a scripting statement, runs the statements of the first matching WHEN branch.

name: CASE expr
description: Compares one expression with the value in each WHEN clause in order and returns the result of the first equal match, otherwise the ELSE result or NULL.

name: CAST
description: Converts an expression to a specified data type and raises an error if the value cannot be converted.

name: CAST AS ARRAY
description: Converts an array into an array of a different element type, which works when each element type can itself be cast to the target element type.

name: CAST AS BIGNUMERIC
description: Converts a number or a string into BIGNUMERIC, the high-precision decimal type, raising an error if the value cannot be converted.

name: CAST AS BOOL
description: Converts an integer or a string into BOOL: zero becomes FALSE and any other integer TRUE; the strings true and false are accepted in any letter case.

name: CAST AS BYTES
description: Converts a STRING into BYTES using its UTF-8 encoding, optionally with a format clause such as base64 decoding.

name: CAST AS DATE
description: Converts a STRING, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP into a DATE; a timestamp is truncated to its date in the default time zone and an invalid string raises an error.

name: CAST AS DATETIME
description: Converts a STRING, DATE or TIMESTAMP into a DATETIME, which holds a calendar date and a time of day without a time zone.

name: CAST AS FLOAT64
description: Converts an integer, decimal or string into FLOAT64; integers may lose exactness, and strings such as inf, -inf and nan are read as special values.

name: CAST AS INT64
description: Converts a number, BOOL or string into INT64; floating point values round to the closest integer with halves rounding away from zero, and hex strings are accepted.

name: CAST AS INTERVAL
description: Converts a STRING into an INTERVAL value; the string must follow an accepted interval text format, otherwise an error is raised.

name: CAST AS NUMERIC
description: Converts an integer, floating point value or string into NUMERIC, the exact decimal type, raising an error if the value cannot be represented.

name: CAST AS RANGE
description: Converts a STRING in range literal form, such as a pair of dates in brackets, into a RANGE value; invalid strings raise an error.

name: CAST AS STRING
description: Converts a value of nearly any type, such as numbers, dates, BYTES or BOOL, into its STRING text form, optionally using a format clause.

name: CAST AS STRUCT
description: Converts a struct into another struct type when both have the same number of fields and each field can be cast to the matching target field by position.

name: CAST AS TIME
description: Converts a STRING, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP into a TIME of day; the string must match the time literal format or an error is raised.

name: CAST AS TIMESTAMP
description: Converts a STRING, DATE or DATETIME into a TIMESTAMP, a point in time; dates and datetimes are read in the default time zone and an invalid string raises an error.

name: COALESCE
description: Returns the value of the first expression in its argument list that is not NULL, or NULL if every argument is NULL.

name: Expression list
description: Overview list of the conditional expressions, such as CASE, COALESCE, IF, IFNULL and NULLIF, each with a one-line summary of what it returns.

name: Function list
description: Overview list of the conversion functions, such as CAST, SAFE_CAST and the number parsing functions, each with a one-line summary.

name: IF
description: As a function, IF returns one of two values depending on a condition; as a scripting statement, IF runs the first block of statements whose condition is true, with optional ELSEIF and ELSE blocks.

name: IFNULL
description: Returns its first argument if that is not NULL, and otherwise returns the second argument.

name: NULLIF
description: Returns NULL when its two arguments are equal, and otherwise returns the first argument.

name: SAFE_CAST
description: Converts an expression to a specified data type like CAST, but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the conversion fails.

name: Arithmetic operators
description: Operators for numeric math: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and unary plus and minus, where the result generally has the same type as the operands.

name: ARRAY_AGG
description: Aggregate function that returns an array of the values from the input rows, with optional DISTINCT, NULL handling, ordering and a limit on the number of elements.
notes: ARRAY_AGG as an analytic function (OVER (...)) is refused (asserted); an ARRAY_AGG over NUMERIC values cannot be written to a destination table (asserted).

name: Array construction
description: Builds an array value from a list of elements, written as ARRAY[1, 2, 3] or just [1, 2, 3], optionally with an explicit element type such as ARRAY<INT64>[1, 2].
notes: An array constructor over computed TIMESTAMP (asserted), INTERVAL (asserted), DATETIME, NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC elements is refused before execution.

name: BETWEEN
description: Checks whether a value lies between a lower and an upper bound, both inclusive, and returns TRUE or FALSE; NOT BETWEEN gives the opposite check.

name: Bitwise operators
description: Operators that work bit by bit on integers or BYTES: bitwise NOT, OR, XOR and AND plus shifts; the result has the same type as the first operand.

name: CASE WHEN
description: Searched form of CASE that evaluates each WHEN condition in order and returns the result of the first one that is TRUE, otherwise the ELSE result or NULL.
notes: CASE results of type DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL or JSON are refused before execution (no compiler contract; the INTERVAL refusal is asserted).

name: CAST / SAFE_CAST
description: CAST converts a value to another type and raises an error when it cannot; SAFE_CAST does the same but returns NULL instead of an error when the conversion fails.
notes: CAST ... FORMAT '...' is refused; a runtime CAST or SAFE_CAST of a STRING value to FLOAT64 is refused (Unqualified cast contract); other casts outside the registered source/target pairs are refused before execution.

name: COALESCE
description: Returns the value of the first expression in its argument list that is not NULL, or NULL if every argument is NULL.
notes: COALESCE over DATETIME values is refused (asserted), as are TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL (asserted) and JSON values, which have no compiler contract.

name: Comparison operators
description: Operators that compare two values and return a BOOL, such as less than, greater than, equal and not equal; ordering comparisons can honor a collation.

name: IF(cond val1 val2)
description: Returns the second argument when the condition is TRUE and the third otherwise, evaluating only the branch that is actually returned.
notes: IF over INTERVAL branch values is refused (asserted); JSON branch values have no compiler contract and are refused.

name: IFNULL
description: Returns its first argument if that is not NULL, and otherwise returns the second argument.
notes: IFNULL over DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL (asserted) or JSON values is refused before execution (no compiler contract).

name: IN list
description: Checks whether a value equals any value in a parenthesized list, returning TRUE on a match; NOT IN reverses the check.
notes: IN lists over DATE, TIME, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP or INTERVAL (asserted) values are refused before execution (no compiler contract).

name: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
description: Checks whether a value is NULL, returning TRUE or FALSE and never NULL itself; IS NOT NULL gives the opposite result.

name: LIKE / NOT LIKE
description: Matches a string against a pattern where a percent sign stands for any run of characters and an underscore for exactly one; NOT LIKE returns the opposite result.

name: Logical operators (AND OR NOT)
description: Combine or negate BOOL values using three-valued logic over TRUE, FALSE and NULL, so a NULL operand can make the result NULL.

name: NULLIF
description: Returns NULL when its two arguments are equal, and otherwise returns the first argument.
notes: NULLIF over DATETIME, TIMESTAMP or INTERVAL (asserted) values is refused before execution (no compiler contract).

name: SAFE.function()
description: Putting the SAFE. prefix before a function name makes that call return NULL instead of raising an error, but it does not hide errors raised while evaluating the arguments.
notes: SAFE. on functions outside the selected families is refused (for example SAFE.UPPER, SAFE.NORMALIZE, SAFE.PARSE_NUMERIC, SAFE.ST_GEOGPOINT, SAFE.JUSTIFY_DAYS, SAFE.TO_JSON, SAFE.HLL_COUNT.EXTRACT, SAFE.KEYS.KEYSET_FROM_JSON); a SAFE call whose operand can raise the same error as the call itself is refused (for example SAFE.LEFT(LEFT('a', -1), 1)); SAFE calls over non-immutable or uncaptured operands are refused.

name: String concatenation (||)
description: Joins two or more STRING values, or two or more BYTES values, end to end into a single value, written with a double vertical bar between the operands.

name: Struct construction
description: Builds a STRUCT value from fields, using tuple syntax such as (1, 'abc'), STRUCT(1 AS a, 'x' AS b), or a typed form like STRUCT<INT64, STRING>(1, 'abc').

name: STRUCT field access (dot notation)
description: Reads a field of a STRUCT by name with a dot, as in my_struct.field_name, and can chain through nested structs.

name: UNNEST
description: Takes an array and returns a table with one row per element, for use in FROM or to flatten arrays; WITH OFFSET adds a column with each element's zero-based position.

name: AVRO
description: Row-oriented binary format that stores its schema alongside the records, so an external table or load can read column names and types from the data itself.

name: Bigtable
description: A Cloud Bigtable table queried in place as an external table, with its column families and columns mapped to BigQuery columns.

name: CSV
description: Comma-separated text data read by an external table or load, with options for the delimiter, quote character, header rows to skip, encoding and null markers.

name: Explicit schema
description: Column names and types spelled out in the table definition rather than inferred from the source data.

name: GCS (gs://)
description: Cloud Storage object paths written as gs://bucket/path, which external tables and load jobs use to locate the data they read.

name: Glob patterns (*)
description: An asterisk wildcard in a Cloud Storage path that lets one external table or load read every object whose name matches the pattern.
notes: '?' and '[...]' in a URI are treated as wildcard patterns rather than literal object-name characters.

name: Google Sheets
description: A Google Sheets spreadsheet queried in place as an external table, optionally limited to a sheet range and with a number of leading rows skipped.

name: Hive partitioning
description: Data laid out in key=value directory names, which an external table or load can expose as partition columns so queries can filter on them.

name: NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON
description: JSON text with one complete JSON object per line, a format that external tables and load jobs can read into rows.

name: ORC
description: Columnar binary format from the Hadoop ecosystem that stores its schema with the data and can be read by external tables and load jobs.

name: PARQUET
description: Columnar binary format that stores the schema with the data and compresses by column, readable by external tables and load jobs.

name: S3
description: Amazon S3 buckets whose data BigQuery reads in place through an external table, using a connection that holds the access credentials.

name: Schema autodetect
description: Lets BigQuery infer column names and types by sampling the source data, instead of requiring the schema to be declared up front.

name: FROM \
description: The FROM clause names the table or other source a query reads; a path with dashes or other special characters is wrapped in backtick quotes.

name: project.dataset.table
description: A fully qualified table name made of project, dataset and table joined by dots, which picks a table in any project from FROM or DML.

name: Subqueries in FROM
description: A parenthesized SELECT placed in the FROM clause, usually with an alias, whose result acts as an input table for the outer query.

name: Table-valued function calls (TVFs)
description: A call to a function in FROM that returns a table, taking arguments and producing rows that can be selected from or joined like any table.

name: ABS
description: Returns the absolute value of a numeric argument, and raises an error if the result cannot be represented in the same type.

name: ACOS
description: Returns the inverse cosine of a number as an angle in radians between 0 and pi, and raises an error if the input is outside the range -1 to 1.

name: ACOSH
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number, and raises an error if the input is less than 1.

name: AEAD.DECRYPT_BYTES
description: Decrypts ciphertext using the matching key in a keyset and checks its integrity against the additional data, returning the original plaintext as BYTES.

name: AEAD.DECRYPT_STRING
description: Decrypts ciphertext using the matching key in a keyset, with additional data of type STRING used to verify integrity, and returns the plaintext as a STRING.

name: AEAD.ENCRYPT
description: Encrypts plaintext with the primary key in a keyset, authenticating it with additional data, and returns the ciphertext as BYTES.

name: AGG
description: Aggregates a measure column, running the calculation that the measure defines once per key so that values are not counted twice.

name: ANY_VALUE
description: Aggregate function that returns the value of an expression from some row of the group; which row is chosen is not specified and can vary between runs.

name: APPENDS
description: Table function that returns the rows inserted into a table during a given time range, with extra columns for the change type and change timestamp.

name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
description: Returns a statistical estimate of the number of distinct values of an expression, less exact than COUNT with DISTINCT but faster on very large inputs.

name: APPROX_QUANTILES
description: Returns an array of approximate quantile boundaries for an expression, running from the approximate minimum to the approximate maximum, for a chosen number of quantiles.

name: APPROX_TOP_COUNT
description: Returns the approximate most frequent values of an expression, with their counts, as an array of structs; a parameter sets how many values to return.

name: APPROX_TOP_SUM
description: Returns the approximate top values of an expression ordered by the sum of a weight for each distinct value, as an array of structs; a parameter sets how many to return.

name: ARRAY
description: Builds an array from a subquery that returns a single column, with one array element for each row of the result.

name: ARRAY_AGG
description: Aggregate function that returns an array of the values from the input rows, with optional DISTINCT, NULL handling, ordering and a limit on the number of elements.

name: ARRAY_CONCAT
description: Joins one or more arrays of the same element type into a single array, keeping the arguments in the order given.

name: ARRAY_CONCAT_AGG
description: Aggregate function that concatenates the array values from the input rows into one array, with optional ordering and a limit on the number of elements.

name: ARRAY_FIRST
description: Returns the first element of an array, and raises an error if the array is empty.

name: ARRAY_LAST
description: Returns the last element of an array, and raises an error if the array is empty.

name: ARRAY_LENGTH
description: Returns the number of elements in an array as an integer: 0 for an empty array and NULL for a NULL array.

name: ARRAY_REVERSE
description: Returns a copy of an array with its elements in reverse order.

name: ARRAY_SLICE
description: Returns the consecutive elements of an array between a start offset and an end offset, both inclusive, where negative offsets count from the end of the array.

name: ARRAY_TO_STRING
description: Joins the elements of a string or bytes array into one value using a delimiter, optionally replacing NULL elements with a given string.

name: ASCII
description: Returns the ASCII code of the first character or byte of a string or bytes value, or 0 if the value is empty.

name: ASIN
description: Returns the inverse sine of a number as an angle in radians between -pi/2 and pi/2, and raises an error if the input is outside the range -1 to 1.

name: ASIN / ACOS / ATAN / ATAN2
description: Inverse trigonometric functions: ASIN, ACOS and ATAN return the angle in radians for a given sine, cosine or tangent, and ATAN2 takes two arguments and uses their signs to pick the quadrant.

name: ASINH
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number, which is the value whose hyperbolic sine equals the input.

name: ATAN
description: Returns the inverse tangent of a number as an angle in radians between -pi/2 and pi/2.

name: ATAN2
description: Returns the inverse tangent of the ratio of two numbers as an angle in radians from -pi to pi, using the signs of both arguments to determine the quadrant.

name: ATANH
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number, and raises an error if the input is outside the range between -1 and 1.

name: AVG
description: Aggregate function that returns the average of the non-NULL values of an expression across the input rows.

name: BAG_OF_WORDS
description: Counts how many times each term appears in a tokenized document and returns an array of structs holding a term and its count.

name: BIT_AND
description: Aggregate function that returns the bitwise AND of an integer or bytes expression across the input rows.

name: BIT_COUNT
description: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in an integer or a BYTES value; for signed integers it counts the bits in two's complement form.

name: BIT_OR
description: Aggregate function that returns the bitwise OR of an integer or bytes expression across the input rows.

name: BIT_XOR
description: Aggregate function that returns the bitwise XOR of an integer or bytes expression across the input rows.

name: BOOL
description: Converts a JSON boolean to a SQL BOOL value, and raises an error if the JSON value is not a boolean.

name: BYTE_LENGTH
description: Returns the number of bytes in a string or bytes value, counting bytes rather than characters even for a STRING.

name: CAST
description: Converts an expression to a specified data type and raises an error if the value cannot be converted.

name: CBRT
description: Returns the cube root of a numeric value, which may be negative.

name: CEIL
description: Rounds a number up and returns the smallest whole number that is not less than the input.

name: CEIL / CEILING
description: Two names for the same rounding function: CEIL and CEILING each return the smallest whole number that is not less than the input.

name: CEILING
description: Synonym for CEIL that rounds a number up to the nearest whole number not less than the input.

name: CHANGES
description: Table function that returns the rows inserted, updated or deleted in a table during a given time range, with extra columns for the change type and change timestamp.

name: CHAR_LENGTH
description: Returns the number of characters in a string value.

name: CHARACTER_LENGTH
description: Synonym for CHAR_LENGTH that returns the number of characters in a string value.

name: CHR
description: Converts a Unicode code point to the character it represents, returning an empty string for 0 and an error for an invalid code point.

name: CODE_POINTS_TO_BYTES
description: Converts an array of extended ASCII code points, given as INT64 values, into a BYTES value.

name: CODE_POINTS_TO_STRING
description: Converts an array of Unicode code points, given as INT64 values, into a STRING.

name: CONCAT
description: Joins one or more string or bytes values end to end into a single value, and returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

name: CONTAINS_SUBSTR
description: Performs a normalized, case-insensitive search and returns TRUE if a value occurs as a substring of an expression such as a string, a column or a whole row.

name: CORR
description: Aggregate function that returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of a set of number pairs.

name: COS
description: Returns the cosine of an angle that is given in radians.

name: COSH
description: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number, and raises an error if the result overflows.

name: COSINE_DISTANCE
description: Computes the cosine distance between two vectors, given as arrays of numbers or as sparse arrays of dimension and magnitude structs.

name: COT
description: Returns the cotangent of an angle that is given in radians.

name: COTH
description: Returns the hyperbolic cotangent of a number that is given in radians.

name: COUNT
description: Aggregate function that counts the input rows, or counts the rows where an expression is not NULL, optionally counting only distinct values.

name: COUNTIF
description: Aggregate function that returns the number of rows for which a boolean expression evaluates to TRUE.

name: COVAR_POP
description: Aggregate function that returns the population covariance of a set of number pairs.

name: COVAR_SAMP
description: Aggregate function that returns the sample covariance of a set of number pairs.

name: CSC
description: Returns the cosecant of an angle that is given in radians.

name: CSCH
description: Returns the hyperbolic cosecant of a number that is given in radians.

name: CUME_DIST
description: Window function that returns, for each row, the fraction of rows in its ordered partition that come before it or tie with it, a value above 0 and up to 1.

name: CURRENT_DATE
description: Returns the current date as a DATE value, using UTC unless a time zone expression is given.

name: CURRENT_DATETIME
description: Returns the current date and time as a DATETIME value with no time zone attached, in UTC unless a time zone is given.

name: CURRENT_TIME
description: Returns the current time of day as a TIME value, in UTC unless a time zone is given.

name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
description: Returns the current date and time as a TIMESTAMP value, a precise point in time that does not depend on a time zone.

name: DATE
description: As a function, DATE builds a DATE from year, month and day values or from a timestamp or datetime; as a type, DATE holds a calendar date with no time of day or time zone.

name: DATE_ADD
description: Adds a number of date parts, such as days, weeks, months or years, to a DATE and returns the resulting DATE.

name: DATE_BUCKET
description: Returns the start date of the fixed-width bucket that contains a date, where the bucket width is an interval and an origin date can be set.

name: DATE_DIFF
description: Returns the number of date part boundaries, such as days, weeks or months, between two dates at the granularity you choose.

name: DATE_FROM_UNIX_DATE
description: Converts an integer count of days since 1970-01-01 into a DATE.

name: DATE_SUB
description: Subtracts a number of date parts, such as days, weeks, months or years, from a DATE and returns the resulting DATE.

name: DATE_TRUNC
description: Truncates a date down to the start of a given date part, such as week, month, quarter or year, and returns a DATE.

name: DATETIME
description: As a function, DATETIME builds a DATETIME from date and time parts, from a date and optional time, or from a timestamp; as a type, DATETIME holds a calendar date and time of day with no time zone.

name: DATETIME_ADD
description: Adds a number of date and time parts, such as days, hours or minutes, to a DATETIME and returns the resulting DATETIME.

name: DATETIME_BUCKET
description: Returns the start of the fixed-width bucket that contains a datetime, where the bucket width is an interval and an origin datetime can be set.

name: DATETIME_DIFF
description: Returns the number of date or time part boundaries, such as days, hours or minutes, between two DATETIME values at the granularity you choose.

name: DATETIME_SUB
description: Subtracts a number of date and time parts, such as days, hours or minutes, from a DATETIME and returns the resulting DATETIME.

name: DATETIME_TRUNC
description: Truncates a DATETIME down to the start of a given date or time part, such as day, hour, week or month, and returns a DATETIME.

name: DENSE_RANK
description: Window function that returns the rank of each row in its ordered partition, giving tied rows the same rank and leaving no gaps between consecutive ranks.

name: DESTINATION_NODE_ID
description: Returns a unique identifier for the destination node of a graph edge, valid only within the query that produces it.

name: DETERMINISTIC_DECRYPT_BYTES
description: Decrypts ciphertext made with deterministic AEAD encryption, using the matching key in a keyset and the additional data, and returns the plaintext as BYTES.

name: DETERMINISTIC_DECRYPT_STRING
description: Decrypts ciphertext made with deterministic AEAD encryption, using the matching key in a keyset and the additional data, and returns the plaintext as a STRING.

name: DETERMINISTIC_ENCRYPT
description: Encrypts plaintext with the primary key in a keyset using deterministic AEAD, so the same plaintext, key and additional data always produce the same ciphertext.

name: DIV
description: Returns the result of integer division of one number by another, and raises an error on division by zero.

name: DLP_DETERMINISTIC_DECRYPT
description: Decrypts a string made by DLP deterministic encryption, using a data key derived from a key chain and an optional context, and returns the plaintext as a STRING.

name: DLP_DETERMINISTIC_ENCRYPT
description: Encrypts a string deterministically with a data key derived from a key chain and an optional context, can prepend a surrogate string, and returns the result as a STRING.

name: DLP_KEY_CHAIN
description: Builds the key argument for the DLP deterministic functions from a Cloud KMS key name and a wrapped key, so queries do not contain plaintext keys.

name: EDGES
description: Returns the edges of a graph path as an array, in the same order as they appear in the path.

name: EDIT_DISTANCE
description: Computes the Levenshtein edit distance between two STRING values or two BYTES values, with an optional maximum distance that caps the result.

name: ELEMENT_ID
description: Returns a unique identifier for a graph node or edge, valid only within the query that produces it.

name: ENDS_WITH
description: Returns TRUE if a string or bytes value ends with a given suffix.

name: ERROR
description: Stops the query with a runtime error that carries a given message, so a query can fail on purpose when it meets bad data.

name: EUCLIDEAN_DISTANCE
description: Computes the Euclidean distance between two vectors, given as arrays of numbers or as sparse arrays of dimension and magnitude structs.

name: EXP
description: Returns e raised to the power of a number, the natural exponential, and raises an error if the result overflows.

name: EXTERNAL_QUERY
description: Runs a query written in the SQL dialect of an external database over a connection and returns the result as a temporary table.

name: EXTRACT
description: Returns a single part, such as the year, month, day, hour or week, from a date, datetime, time, timestamp or interval value.

name: FARM_FINGERPRINT
description: Computes the FarmHash Fingerprint64 fingerprint of a string or bytes value and returns it as an INT64; the result for a given input never changes.

name: FILTER
description: In graph queries, FILTER keeps only the rows of the working table for which a boolean condition is TRUE and drops rows where it is FALSE or NULL.

name: FIRST_VALUE
description: Window function that returns the value of an expression from the first row of the current window frame.

name: FLOOR
description: Rounds a number down and returns the largest whole number that is not greater than the input.

name: FOR
description: In graph queries FOR unnests an array into rows; in scripting FOR...IN loops over the rows of a query result; in FROM, FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF reads a table as it was at an earlier time.

name: FORMAT
description: Builds a string from a format string containing percent specifiers, such as %d, %s and %t, and the values that fill them.

name: FORMAT_DATE
description: Formats a DATE as a string using a format string made of elements such as %Y, %m and %d.

name: FORMAT_DATE
description: Formats a DATE as a string using a format string made of elements such as %Y, %m and %d.
notes: The format string must be a literal (a column, parameter, subquery or computed format is refused); some format elements such as %J are refused; formats longer than 4096 UTF-8 bytes are refused.

name: FORMAT_DATETIME
description: Formats a DATETIME as a string using a format string made of date and time elements such as %Y, %m, %d and %H.

name: FORMAT_DATETIME
description: Formats a DATETIME as a string using a format string made of date and time elements such as %Y, %m, %d and %H.
notes: Format elements the emulator's temporal kernel does not implement (for example %E10S) are refused before execution.

name: FORMAT (printf-style)
description: Printf-style string formatting: a format string with percent specifiers that control type, width, precision and flags is filled in with the remaining arguments to produce a string.
notes: FORMAT with an INTERVAL argument is refused before execution (asserted).

name: FORMAT_TIME
description: Formats a TIME as a string using a format string made of time elements such as %H, %M and %S.

name: FORMAT_TIME
description: Formats a TIME as a string using a format string made of time elements such as %H, %M and %S.
notes: The format string must be a literal (a column, parameter or computed format is refused); some format elements are refused.

name: FORMAT_TIMESTAMP
description: Formats a TIMESTAMP as a string using a format string of date and time elements, with an optional time zone for the display.

name: FORMAT_TIMESTAMP
description: Formats a TIMESTAMP as a string using a format string of date and time elements, with an optional time zone for the display.
notes: Format elements the emulator's temporal kernel does not implement (for example %E10S) are refused before execution.

name: FROM_BASE32
description: Decodes a base32-encoded string into BYTES; the reverse of TO_BASE32.

name: FROM_BASE64
description: Decodes a base64-encoded string into BYTES; the reverse of TO_BASE64.

name: FROM_HEX
description: Converts a hexadecimal-encoded string into BYTES, and raises an error if the string contains characters other than hex digits.

name: GAP_FILL
description: Table function that finds and fills gaps in a time series, adding rows for missing time buckets and filling values with NULL, linear interpolation or the last observed value.

name: GENERATE_ARRAY
description: Returns an array of numbers from a start value to an end value, advancing by an optional step.

name: GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY
description: Returns an array of dates from a start date to an end date, advancing by an interval of days, weeks, months or years.

name: GENERATE_RANGE_ARRAY
description: Splits a RANGE value into an array of consecutive subranges, each as wide as a given step interval.

name: GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY
description: Returns an array of timestamps from a start timestamp to an end timestamp, advancing by an interval such as seconds, minutes, hours or days.

name: GENERATE_UUID
description: Returns a randomly generated universally unique identifier (UUID) as a STRING of 32 hexadecimal digits in hyphen-separated groups.

name: GQL
description: Graph Query Language syntax for querying a property graph: a chain of statements such as MATCH, FILTER, LET and RETURN, each passing its result table to the next.

name: GRAPH_TABLE
description: Operator used in the FROM clause that runs a graph query against a property graph and returns the result as a table the rest of the SQL query can use.

name: GREATEST
description: Returns the largest value among its arguments, and returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

name: GROUPING
description: Returns 1 if a grouping item in GROUP BY is aggregated in the current output row, as in a ROLLUP or CUBE subtotal row, and 0 otherwise.

name: HLL_COUNT.EXTRACT
description: Scalar function that returns the cardinality estimate, the approximate distinct count, held in a single HLL++ sketch.

name: HLL_COUNT.INIT
description: Aggregate function that collects input values into an HLL++ sketch, returned as BYTES, which can be merged later or turned into a distinct count estimate.

name: HLL_COUNT.MERGE
description: Aggregate function that merges several HLL++ sketches by taking their union and returns the resulting estimate of the number of distinct values.

name: HLL_COUNT.MERGE_PARTIAL
description: Aggregate function that merges several HLL++ sketches into one new sketch, returned as BYTES, that can be merged again later.

name: IEEE_DIVIDE
description: Divides two numbers and returns infinity or NaN instead of raising an error when the divisor is zero or the result overflows.

name: IF
description: As a function, IF returns one of two values depending on a condition; as a scripting statement, IF runs the first block of statements whose condition is true, with optional ELSEIF and ELSE blocks.
notes: IF over INTERVAL branch values is refused (asserted); JSON branch values have no compiler contract and are refused.

name: INITCAP
description: Returns a string with the first character of each word in uppercase and the rest in lowercase, with optional custom word delimiters.

name: INSTR
description: Returns the 1-based position of a substring within a string or bytes value, with an optional start position and occurrence, or 0 if it is not found.

name: IS_FIRST
description: Window function that returns TRUE when the current row is among the first k rows of its partition, in the window ordering, and FALSE otherwise.

name: IS_INF
description: Returns TRUE if a number is positive or negative infinity.

name: IS_NAN
description: Returns TRUE if a floating-point number is NaN, meaning not a number.

name: JSON_ARRAY
description: Creates a JSON array from zero or more SQL values.

name: JSON_ARRAY_APPEND
description: Appends values to the end of the arrays found at given JSON paths in a JSON value, and returns the updated JSON.

name: JSON_ARRAY_INSERT
description: Inserts values into the arrays found at given JSON paths, at the array position named in each path, and returns the updated JSON.

name: JSON_EXTRACT
description: Extracts the value at a JSON path from a JSON or JSON-formatted string input and returns it as JSON text; an older function that JSON_QUERY replaces.

name: JSON_EXTRACT_ARRAY
description: Extracts the JSON array at a JSON path and returns it as an array of JSON values or JSON-formatted strings; an older function that JSON_QUERY_ARRAY replaces.

name: JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR
description: Extracts the scalar value at a JSON path and returns it as a STRING without quotes; an older function that JSON_VALUE replaces.

name: JSON_EXTRACT_STRING_ARRAY
description: Extracts the array of scalar values at a JSON path and returns it as an ARRAY of STRING values; an older function that JSON_VALUE_ARRAY replaces.

name: JSON_FLATTEN
description: Returns an array of all the non-array values in a JSON value, flattening arrays that are nested directly inside other arrays.

name: JSON_KEYS
description: Extracts the unique keys from a JSON value and returns them as an array of strings.

name: JSON_OBJECT
description: Creates a JSON object from key and value pairs, or from an array of keys and an array of values.

name: JSON_QUERY
description: Extracts the JSON value at a JSON path from a JSON or JSON-formatted string input and returns it as JSON or as JSON text.

name: JSON_QUERY_ARRAY
description: Extracts the JSON array at a JSON path and returns it as an array of JSON values, or of JSON-formatted strings when given a string.

name: JSON_REMOVE
description: Removes the data at one or more JSON paths from a JSON value and returns the new JSON value.

name: JSON_SET
description: Inserts or replaces data at one or more JSON paths in a JSON value and returns the new JSON value.

name: JSON_STRIP_NULLS
description: Recursively removes JSON null values from the objects, and optionally the arrays, of a JSON value and returns the result.

name: JSON_TYPE
description: Returns the type of the outermost JSON value as a STRING, such as object, array, string, number, boolean or null.

name: JSON_VALUE
description: Extracts the scalar value at a JSON path from a JSON or JSON-formatted string input and returns it as a STRING, or NULL if the value is not a scalar.

name: JSON_VALUE_ARRAY
description: Extracts the JSON array of scalar values at a JSON path and returns it as an ARRAY of STRING values, or NULL if the value is not such an array.

name: JUSTIFY_DAYS
description: Normalizes the days part of an interval to the range -29 to 29 by adding to or subtracting from the month part, and returns an INTERVAL.

name: JUSTIFY_HOURS
description: Normalizes the time part of an interval to under 24 hours in either direction by carrying whole days into the day part, and returns an INTERVAL.

name: JUSTIFY_INTERVAL
description: Normalizes the days and time parts of an interval by moving overflow into the next larger part, such as hours into days and days into months, and returns an INTERVAL.

name: KEYS.ADD_KEY_FROM_RAW_BYTES
description: Adds a key built from raw key bytes and a key type to a keyset and returns the updated serialized keyset as BYTES.

name: KEYS.KEYSET_CHAIN
description: Builds a keyset argument for the encryption functions from a Cloud KMS key name and a keyset that is encrypted with that key, so queries do not contain plaintext keysets.

name: KEYS.KEYSET_FROM_JSON
description: Converts a keyset written as a JSON string into a serialized keyset in BYTES that the KEYS and AEAD functions accept.

name: KEYS.KEYSET_LENGTH
description: Returns the number of keys in a keyset as an INT64.

name: KEYS.KEYSET_TO_JSON
description: Returns the contents of a keyset as a JSON-formatted STRING, the reverse of converting a JSON keyset into serialized BYTES.

name: KEYS.NEW_KEYSET
description: Creates a new keyset that holds one new key of a chosen key type and returns it serialized as BYTES.

name: KEYS.NEW_WRAPPED_KEYSET
description: Creates a new keyset with a key of a chosen type, encrypts it with a Cloud KMS key, and returns the wrapped keyset as BYTES.

name: KEYS.REWRAP_KEYSET
description: Re-encrypts a wrapped keyset, decrypting with the source Cloud KMS key and encrypting with a target Cloud KMS key, and returns the new wrapped keyset as BYTES.

name: KEYS.ROTATE_KEYSET
description: Adds a new key of a chosen key type to a keyset and returns the updated serialized keyset as BYTES.

name: KEYS.ROTATE_WRAPPED_KEYSET
description: Takes an existing wrapped keyset, adds a new key of a chosen type, rewraps it with a Cloud KMS key, and returns the rotated wrapped keyset as BYTES.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.EXTRACT_FLOAT64
description: Returns an array of approximate quantiles from a KLL sketch built over FLOAT64 values, for a chosen number of quantiles.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.EXTRACT_INT64
description: Returns an array of approximate quantiles from a KLL sketch built over INT64 values, for a chosen number of quantiles.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.EXTRACT_POINT_FLOAT64
description: Returns the approximate FLOAT64 value at one quantile position, given as a fraction between 0 and 1, from a KLL sketch.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.EXTRACT_POINT_INT64
description: Returns the approximate INT64 value at one quantile position, given as a fraction between 0 and 1, from a KLL sketch.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.INIT_FLOAT64
description: Aggregate function that collects FLOAT64 values, with optional precision and weight, into a KLL sketch returned as BYTES.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.INIT_INT64
description: Aggregate function that collects INT64 values, with optional precision and weight, into a KLL sketch returned as BYTES.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.MERGE_FLOAT64
description: Aggregate function that merges KLL sketches built over FLOAT64 values and returns an array of approximate quantiles of the combined data.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.MERGE_INT64
description: Aggregate function that merges KLL sketches built over INT64 values and returns an array of approximate quantiles of the combined data.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.MERGE_PARTIAL
description: Aggregate function that merges KLL sketches of the same value type into a new sketch, returned as BYTES, that can be merged or queried later.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.MERGE_POINT_FLOAT64
description: Aggregate function that merges KLL sketches built over FLOAT64 values and returns the approximate value at one quantile position between 0 and 1.

name: KLL_QUANTILES.MERGE_POINT_INT64
description: Aggregate function that merges KLL sketches built over INT64 values and returns the approximate value at one quantile position between 0 and 1.

name: LABELS
description: Returns the labels of a graph node or edge as an array of strings, keeping the original case of each label.

name: LAG
description: Window function that returns the value of an expression from a preceding row, by default the previous row, with an optional offset and default value.

name: LAST_DAY
description: Returns the last day of the month for a date, or of another date part such as the week, quarter or year when one is given.

name: LAST_VALUE
description: Window function that returns the value of an expression from the last row of the current window frame.

name: LAX_BOOL
description: Converts a JSON value to a SQL BOOL, accepting JSON booleans, the strings true and false in any case, and numbers where 0 is FALSE; other values return NULL.

name: LAX_FLOAT64
description: Converts a JSON number, or a JSON string that holds a number, to a FLOAT64 value, and returns NULL for values that cannot be converted.

name: LAX_INT64
description: Converts a JSON boolean, number or numeric string to an INT64 value, mapping true to 1 and false to 0, and returns NULL for values that cannot be converted.

name: LAX_STRING
description: Converts a JSON string, number or boolean to a STRING value, and returns NULL for other JSON types.

name: LEAD
description: Window function that returns the value of an expression from a following row, by default the next row, with an optional offset and default value.

name: LEAST
description: Returns the smallest value among its arguments, and returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

name: LEFT
description: Returns the leftmost characters of a string, or the leftmost bytes of a bytes value, up to a given length.

name: LENGTH
description: Returns the length of a string in characters or of a bytes value in bytes.

name: LET
description: In graph queries, LET defines variables and assigns them values computed from the working table, for use by later statements in the same linear query.

name: LIMIT
description: Limits a query to at most a given number of rows; in graph queries, the LIMIT statement likewise caps the number of rows passed on to the next statement.

name: LN
description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number, and raises an error if the number is zero or negative.

name: LOG
description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number when given one argument, or the logarithm of the first argument to the base of the second argument.

name: LOG10
description: Returns the base 10 logarithm of a number, and raises an error if the number is zero or negative.

name: LOGICAL_AND
description: Aggregate function that returns TRUE if the boolean expression is TRUE in every non-NULL input row, and NULL if there are no such rows.

name: LOGICAL_OR
description: Aggregate function that returns TRUE if the boolean expression is TRUE in at least one input row, and NULL if there are no non-NULL rows.

name: LOWER
description: Returns a string with all alphabetic characters converted to lowercase, or a bytes value treated as ASCII text with its letters lowercased.

name: LPAD
description: Pads a string or bytes value on the left with a repeating pattern until it reaches a given length, or shortens it to that length.

name: LTRIM
description: Removes leading characters from a string or bytes value, either whitespace or any characters from a given set.

name: MAKE_INTERVAL
description: Builds an INTERVAL value from integer year, month, day, hour, minute and second arguments, each of which is optional.

name: MATCH
description: In graph queries, MATCH finds the paths in a property graph that fit a pattern of nodes and edges; OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the row and fills unmatched parts of the pattern with NULL.

name: MAX
description: Aggregate function that returns the maximum value of an expression across the input rows, ignoring NULL values.

name: MAX_BY
description: Aggregate function that returns the value of one expression from the row where a second expression has its maximum value.

name: MD5
description: Computes the MD5 hash of a string or bytes value and returns the 16-byte digest as BYTES; MD5 is no longer considered secure.

name: MIN
description: Aggregate function that returns the minimum value of an expression across the input rows, ignoring NULL values.

name: MIN_BY
description: Aggregate function that returns the value of one expression from the row where a second expression has its minimum value.

name: MOD
description: Returns the remainder of dividing one number by another, with the sign of the first number, and raises an error if the divisor is 0.

name: NET.HOST
description: Takes a URL string and returns its host part, such as the domain name or IP address, or NULL if the host cannot be parsed from the input.

name: NET.IP_FROM_STRING
description: Converts an IPv4 or IPv6 address from text to a BYTES value in network byte order, raising an error when the text is not a valid address.

name: NET.IP_NET_MASK
description: Returns a network mask as BYTES of the given length, 4 for IPv4 or 16 for IPv6, with the first prefix_length bits set to 1 and the rest set to 0.

name: NET.IP_TO_STRING
description: Converts an IPv4 or IPv6 address from BYTES in network byte order to text; 4-byte input gives an IPv4 string and 16-byte input gives an IPv6 string.

name: NET.IP_TRUNC
description: Takes an IPv4 or IPv6 address as BYTES and a prefix length and returns the subnet address, keeping the first prefix_length bits and zeroing the rest.

name: NET.IPV4_FROM_INT64
description: Converts an IPv4 address from an INT64 value to BYTES in network byte order, so that the integer 1 becomes the address 0.0.0.1.

name: NET.IPV4_TO_INT64
description: Converts an IPv4 address from BYTES in network byte order to an INT64 value, so that the address 0.0.0.1 becomes the integer 1.

name: NET.PUBLIC_SUFFIX
description: Takes a URL string and returns its public suffix, such as com, org or net, or NULL when the host has no public suffix.

name: NET.REG_DOMAIN
description: Takes a URL string and returns its registered domain, which is the public suffix plus one preceding label, or NULL when there is none.

name: NET.SAFE_IP_FROM_STRING
description: Converts an IPv4 or IPv6 address from text to BYTES in network byte order, returning NULL instead of an error when the text is not a valid address.

name: NEXT
description: In a graph query, chains linear query statements together so that the columns returned by one statement can be used by the statement that follows.

name: NODES
description: Takes a graph path and returns an array of the nodes in it, in the same order as they appear in the path.

name: NORMALIZE
description: Takes a string and returns it in a Unicode normalization form, NFC by default, so that strings that render the same have the same code points.

name: NORMALIZE_AND_CASEFOLD
description: Normalizes a string to a Unicode normalization form and case-folds it, which prepares text for comparisons that ignore case and character composition.

name: NTH_VALUE
description: Window function that returns the value of an expression at the Nth row of the current window frame, or NULL if the frame has no such row.

name: NTILE
description: Window function that divides the ordered rows of a partition into a given number of buckets and returns each row's bucket number, starting at 1.

name: OBJ.FETCH_METADATA
description: Fetches Cloud Storage metadata for an ObjectRef value that has only its URI set and returns a fully populated ObjectRef value.

name: OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL
description: Takes an ObjectRef and an access mode, read or read-write, and returns a JSON value with the object reference and time-limited access URLs for the Cloud Storage object.

name: OBJ.GET_READ_URL
description: Takes an ObjectRef and returns a struct holding a time-limited read URL for the Cloud Storage object, plus a status field that carries any error message.

name: OBJ.MAKE_REF
description: Creates an ObjectRef value that points to a Cloud Storage object from its URI, optionally with a connection authorizer, a version and metadata.

name: OCTET_LENGTH
description: Returns the length of a STRING or BYTES value in bytes; it is an alias for BYTE_LENGTH.

name: OFFSET
description: Skips rows: the OFFSET clause after LIMIT, and the OFFSET statement in graph queries. Also OFFSET(index) picks an array element by zero-based position.

name: PARSE_BIGNUMERIC
description: Converts a string such as 123.45 or 123.456E37 to a BIGNUMERIC value, raising an error if the number is outside the range of BIGNUMERIC.

name: PARSE_DATE
description: Converts a date string to a DATE value, using a format string that describes how the date is laid out in the text.

name: PARSE_DATETIME
description: Converts a datetime string to a DATETIME value, using a format string that describes how the date and time are laid out in the text.

name: PARSE_JSON
description: Converts a JSON-formatted STRING to a JSON value, with an option for how to handle numbers that cannot be stored without losing precision.

name: PARSE_NUMERIC
description: Converts a string such as 123.45 or 12.34E27 to a NUMERIC value, raising an error if the number is outside the range of NUMERIC.

name: PARSE_TIME
description: Converts a time string to a TIME value, using a format string that describes how the time is laid out in the text.

name: PARSE_TIMESTAMP
description: Converts a timestamp string to a TIMESTAMP value, using a format string that describes the text and an optional time zone.

name: PATH_FIRST
description: Takes a graph path and returns the first node in it, where a path is an alternating sequence of nodes and edges.

name: PATH_LAST
description: Takes a graph path and returns the last node in it, where a path is an alternating sequence of nodes and edges.

name: PATH_LENGTH
description: Takes a graph path and returns the number of edges in it, which is the length of the path.

name: PERCENT_RANK
description: Window function that returns the relative rank of each row in its partition as a value from 0 to 1, calculated as (rank minus 1) divided by (rows minus 1).

name: PERCENTILE_CONT
description: Computes the given percentile of a value expression over a window, using linear interpolation between the two nearest values, and ignores NULLs by default.

name: PERCENTILE_DISC
description: Computes the given percentile of a value expression over a window and returns an actual input value: the first sorted value whose cumulative distribution reaches the percentile.

name: POW
description: Returns the first number raised to the power of the second number.

name: POW / POWER
description: POW and POWER are synonyms: each takes two numbers and returns the first raised to the power of the second.

name: POWER
description: Synonym for POW: takes two numbers X and Y and returns X raised to the power of Y.

name: RAND
description: Takes no arguments and generates a pseudo-random FLOAT64 value that is at least 0 and less than 1.

name: RANGE
description: Constructs a range value from a lower and an upper bound of type DATE, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP; the lower bound is included and the upper bound is not.

name: RANGE_BUCKET
description: Takes a point and a sorted array of boundary values and returns the 0-based index of the first boundary greater than the point, which groups values into buckets.

name: RANGE_CONTAINS
description: Checks whether one range completely contains another range, or whether a single value falls inside a range, and returns TRUE or FALSE.

name: RANGE_END
description: Returns the upper bound of a range, or NULL if the range has no upper bound.

name: RANGE_INTERSECT
description: Returns the segment where two ranges overlap as a range; it raises an error if they do not overlap unless called with the SAFE prefix.

name: RANGE_OVERLAPS
description: Checks whether two ranges of the same type overlap and returns TRUE or FALSE.

name: RANGE_SESSIONIZE
description: Table function that takes a table, a range column and optional partitioning columns and groups rows whose ranges meet or overlap into sessions, adding a session_range column.

name: RANGE_START
description: Returns the lower bound of a range, or NULL if the range has no lower bound.

name: RANK
description: Window function that returns the rank of each row within its ordered partition, giving tied rows the same rank and leaving gaps after ties.

name: REGEXP_CONTAINS
description: Returns TRUE if a string or bytes value matches a regular expression anywhere within it, and FALSE otherwise.

name: REGEXP_EXTRACT
description: Returns the first substring of a value that matches a regular expression, or the text of its capturing group, and NULL if nothing matches.

name: REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL
description: Returns an array of all non-overlapping substrings that match a regular expression, or of the capturing group matches, and an empty array if nothing matches.

name: REGEXP_INSTR
description: Returns the 1-based position of a regular expression match in a string or bytes value, with optional start position and occurrence number, and 0 if there is no match.

name: REGEXP_REPLACE
description: Returns a string or bytes value in which every substring that matches a regular expression is replaced with a replacement value.

name: REGEXP_SUBSTR
description: Synonym for REGEXP_EXTRACT: returns the substring of a value that matches a regular expression, with optional start position and occurrence number.

name: REPEAT
description: As a string function, returns a string or bytes value repeated a given number of times. As a scripting statement, runs a block of statements repeatedly until a condition becomes true.

name: REPLACE
description: Replaces every occurrence of one substring or byte sequence with another in a string or bytes value and returns the result.

name: RETURN
description: In a graph query, ends a linear query statement and returns the result columns, with optional grouping, ordering and limits. In a script, stops execution of the script.

name: REVERSE
description: Returns a STRING or BYTES value with its characters or bytes in reverse order.

name: RIGHT
description: Returns the rightmost given number of characters of a STRING value, or the rightmost bytes of a BYTES value.

name: ROUND
description: Rounds a number to the nearest integer, or to a given number of decimal places, with halfway cases rounded away from zero.

name: ROW_NUMBER
description: Window function that returns the sequential number of each row within its ordered partition, starting at 1.

name: RPAD
description: Returns a string or bytes value padded on the right with a pattern, or with spaces by default, until it reaches a given length.

name: RTRIM
description: Removes the given set of characters, or whitespace by default, from the end of a string or bytes value and returns the result.

name: S2_CELLIDFROMPOINT
description: Returns the S2 cell ID, as an INT64, that covers a point geography at an optional cell level.

name: S2_COVERINGCELLIDS
description: Returns an array of S2 cell IDs that cover a geography, with optional limits on cell levels and number of cells and an optional buffer in meters.
notes: Multi-point, multi-linestring and mixed collections, and buffers on non-point values, are refused.

name: SAFE_ADD
description: Adds two numbers like the plus operator but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the result overflows.

name: SAFE_CAST
description: Converts an expression to a specified data type like CAST, but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the conversion fails.

name: SAFE_CONVERT_BYTES_TO_STRING
description: Converts a BYTES value to a STRING and replaces any invalid UTF-8 sequences with the Unicode replacement character instead of failing.

name: SAFE_DIVIDE
description: Divides one number by another like the division operator but returns NULL instead of an error when the divisor is zero or the result overflows.

name: SAFE_MULTIPLY
description: Multiplies two numbers like the multiplication operator but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the result overflows.

name: SAFE_NEGATE
description: Negates a number like the unary minus operator but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the result overflows.

name: SAFE_SUBTRACT
description: Subtracts one number from another like the minus operator but returns NULL instead of raising an error when the result overflows.

name: SEARCH
description: Checks whether a table, column or JSON value contains all the terms of a search query, with optional text analyzer settings, and returns TRUE or FALSE.

name: SEC
description: Takes an angle given in radians and returns its secant, which is the reciprocal of the cosine.

name: SECH
description: Returns the hyperbolic secant of an angle given in radians.

name: SESSION_USER
description: Takes no arguments and returns the email address of the user running the query, or the principal identifier for third-party identities.

name: SHA1
description: Computes the SHA-1 hash of a STRING or BYTES value and returns it as 20 bytes; SHA-1 is no longer considered secure.

name: SHA256
description: Computes the SHA-256 hash of a STRING or BYTES value and returns it as 32 bytes.

name: SHA512
description: Computes the SHA-512 hash of a STRING or BYTES value and returns it as 64 bytes.

name: SIGN
description: Returns -1, 0 or 1 when a number is negative, zero or positive.

name: SIN
