description: Takes an angle given in radians and returns its sine as a FLOAT64 value.

name: SIN / COS / TAN
description: Trigonometric functions that each take an angle in radians and return its sine (SIN), cosine (COS) or tangent (TAN).

name: SINH
description: Takes a number and returns its hyperbolic sine as a FLOAT64 value, without raising an error.

name: SINH / COSH / TANH
description: Hyperbolic functions that each take a number and return its hyperbolic sine (SINH), hyperbolic cosine (COSH) or hyperbolic tangent (TANH).

name: SKIP
description: In graph queries, skips a given number of result rows and returns the rest; it is a synonym for the OFFSET statement.

name: SOUNDEX
description: Returns the Soundex code of a string, a letter followed by three digits that reflects English pronunciation, so similar-sounding words get similar codes.

name: SOURCE_NODE_ID
description: Takes a graph edge and returns a unique identifier of its source node, which is only valid within the query that produced it.

name: SPLIT
description: Splits a STRING or BYTES value on a delimiter, a comma by default for strings, and returns an array of the pieces.

name: SQRT
description: Computes the square root of a number and returns an error if the number is negative.

name: ST_ANGLE
description: Takes three point geographies and returns the angle in radians between the line from point 2 to point 1 and the line from point 2 to point 3.

name: ST_AREA
description: Returns the area in square meters covered by the polygons in a geography, and zero for points and lines.

name: ST_ASBINARY
description: Returns the Well-Known Binary (WKB) representation of a geography as a BYTES value.

name: ST_ASGEOJSON
description: Returns the GeoJSON representation of a geography, following RFC 7946, as a string.

name: ST_ASTEXT
description: Returns the Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of a geography as a string.

name: ST_AZIMUTH
description: Takes two point geographies and returns the azimuth in radians of the line from the first to the second, measured clockwise from true North.

name: ST_BOUNDARY
description: Returns a geography made of the boundaries of the input components: the end points of a linestring or the rings of a polygon, and nothing for a point.

name: ST_BOUNDINGBOX
description: Returns a struct that describes the smallest rectangle, aligned to lines of longitude and latitude, that encloses a geography.

name: ST_BUFFER
description: Returns a geography covering every point within a given radius in meters of the input geography, with the number of segments per quarter circle adjustable.

name: ST_BUFFERWITHTOLERANCE
description: Like ST_BUFFER, returns the area within a given radius in meters of a geography, but a tolerance in meters controls how far the result may deviate from the ideal buffer.

name: ST_CENTROID
description: Returns the centroid of a geography as a single point geography, computed from its highest-dimensional components.

name: ST_CENTROID_AGG
description: Aggregate function that returns the centroid of a set of geography values as a single point geography.

name: ST_CLOSESTPOINT
description: Takes two geographies and returns the point on the first one that is closest to the second.

name: ST_CLUSTERDBSCAN
description: Window function that groups geographies into clusters with the DBSCAN algorithm, using a radius in meters and a minimum cluster size, and returns a 0-based cluster number or NULL for noise.

name: ST_CONTAINS
description: Returns TRUE if no point of the second geography lies outside the first and the interiors of the two geographies intersect.

name: ST_CONVEXHULL
description: Returns the convex hull of a geography, which is the smallest convex geography that covers the input.

name: ST_COVEREDBY
description: Returns TRUE if no point of the first geography lies outside the second; it gives the same result as ST_COVERS with the arguments swapped.

name: ST_COVERS
description: Returns TRUE if no point of the second geography lies outside the first, so a geography also covers its own boundary.

name: ST_DIFFERENCE
description: Returns the part of the first geography that does not intersect with the second geography.

name: ST_DIMENSION
description: Returns the dimension of the highest-dimensional element in a geography: 0 for points, 1 for linestrings, 2 for polygons, and -1 when empty.

name: ST_DISJOINT
description: Returns TRUE if two geographies have no point in common; it is the logical negation of ST_INTERSECTS.

name: ST_DISTANCE
description: Returns the shortest distance in meters between two geographies, measured on a sphere by default, with an option to measure on the WGS84 spheroid.

name: ST_DUMP
description: Splits a geography into an array of simple geographies, one per point, linestring or polygon component, optionally keeping only a given dimension.

name: ST_DWITHIN
description: Returns TRUE if some point of the first geography is within a given distance in meters of some point of the second geography.

name: ST_ENDPOINT
description: Returns the last point of a linestring geography as a point geography.

name: ST_EQUALS
description: Returns TRUE if two geographies represent the same set of points, even when their vertices are listed in a different order.

name: ST_EXTENT
description: Aggregate function that returns a struct for the smallest longitude and latitude aligned rectangle that encloses all the input geographies.

name: ST_EXTERIORRING
description: Returns the outermost ring of a polygon geography as a linestring geography.

name: ST_GEOGFROM
description: Converts a STRING or BYTES value in WKT, WKB or GeoJSON form into a geography value.

name: ST_GEOGFROMGEOJSON
description: Converts a GeoJSON string into a geography, with an option to repair polygons that do not follow Open Geospatial Consortium rules.

name: ST_GEOGFROMTEXT
description: Converts a Well-Known Text (WKT) string into a geography, with an option to read polygon vertices in the orientation given.

name: ST_GEOGFROMWKB
description: Converts Well-Known Binary (WKB) data, given as BYTES or a hexadecimal STRING, into a geography value.

name: ST_GEOGPOINT
description: Creates a point geography from a longitude and a latitude given in degrees.

name: ST_GEOGPOINTFROMGEOHASH
description: Takes a GeoHash string and returns a point geography at the center of the bounding box that the GeoHash describes.

name: ST_GEOHASH
description: Takes a single-point geography and returns its GeoHash string, with an optional limit on the number of characters that sets the precision.

name: ST_GEOMETRYTYPE
description: Returns the Open Geospatial Consortium geometry type of a geography as a string with an ST_ prefix, such as ST_Point, ST_LineString or ST_Polygon.

name: ST_HAUSDORFFDISTANCE
description: Returns the discrete Hausdorff distance between two geographies: the greatest of the distances from a point in one geography to the closest point in the other.

name: ST_HAUSDORFFDWITHIN
description: Returns TRUE if the Hausdorff distance between two geographies is less than or equal to a given distance in meters.

name: ST_INTERIORRINGS
description: Returns an array of linestring geographies for the interior rings of a polygon geography, each of which is the border of a hole in the polygon.

name: ST_INTERSECTION
description: Returns the geography made of the points that appear in both input geographies, or an empty geography if they are disjoint.

name: ST_INTERSECTS
description: Returns TRUE if two geographies have at least one point in common.

name: ST_INTERSECTSBOX
description: Returns TRUE if a geography intersects a rectangle bounded by given longitude and latitude values in degrees.

name: ST_ISCLOSED
description: Returns TRUE for a non-empty geography whose elements all have an empty boundary, such as a linestring whose start and end points are the same.

name: ST_ISCOLLECTION
description: Returns TRUE if a geography holds more than one point, linestring or polygon in total; an empty geography is not a collection.

name: ST_ISEMPTY
description: Returns TRUE if a geography contains no points, lines or polygons.

name: ST_ISRING
description: Returns TRUE if a geography is a linestring that is closed and does not pass through the same point twice apart from its start and end points.

name: ST_LENGTH
description: Returns the total length in meters of the lines in a geography, and zero for points and polygons.

name: ST_LINEINTERPOLATEPOINT
description: Returns the point located at a given fraction, from 0 to 1, of the way along a linestring geography.

name: ST_LINELOCATEPOINT
description: Returns the fraction, from 0 to 1, of a linestring's length at which the point on the line closest to a given point lies.

name: ST_LINESUBSTRING
description: Returns the segment of a linestring geography between a start fraction and an end fraction of its total length.

name: ST_MAKELINE
description: Creates a linestring geography by joining the points or line vertices of two geographies, or of an array of geographies, in the order given.

name: ST_MAKEPOLYGON
description: Creates a polygon geography from a linestring that forms the outer shell, optionally with an array of linestrings that form holes.

name: ST_MAKEPOLYGONORIENTED
description: Like ST_MAKEPOLYGON, but the vertex order of each input linestring sets the ring orientation, with the polygon interior on the left as you walk the ring.

name: ST_MAXDISTANCE
description: Returns the longest distance in meters between a vertex of the first geography and a vertex of the second geography.

name: ST_NPOINTS
description: Returns the number of vertices in a geography; it is an alias for ST_NUMPOINTS.

name: ST_NUMGEOMETRIES
description: Returns the number of geometries in a geography: 1 for a single point, linestring or polygon, the collection size for a collection, and 0 if empty.

name: ST_NUMPOINTS
description: Returns the number of vertices in a geography, counting points, linestring vertices and polygon vertices.

name: ST_PERIMETER
description: Returns the length in meters of the boundary of the polygons in a geography, and zero for points and lines.

name: ST_POINTN
description: Returns the Nth point of a linestring geography as a point geography, using a 1-based index where negative values count back from the end.

name: ST_REGIONSTATS
description: Computes statistics, returned as a struct, for the pixels of a geospatial raster image that intersect a geography.

name: ST_SIMPLIFY
description: Returns a simplified geography by replacing nearly straight chains of short edges with single long edges, staying within a tolerance given in meters.

name: ST_SNAPTOGRID
description: Returns a geography in which every vertex is snapped to a longitude and latitude grid whose size is given in degrees.
notes: Only points and empty values are snapped; lines, polygons and multi-part values need S2Builder IntLatLngSnapFunction, which the installed S2 bindings do not expose.

name: ST_STARTPOINT
description: Returns the first point of a linestring geography as a point geography.

name: ST_TOUCHES
description: Returns TRUE if two geographies intersect but their interiors do not, so that they meet only at their boundaries.

name: ST_UNION
description: Returns the geography that is the union of the points of two geographies, or of all the geographies in an array.

name: ST_UNION_AGG
description: Aggregate function that returns the geography formed by the union of the points of all input geographies, ignoring NULLs.
notes: Linestring inputs (BigQuery merges them into one LINESTRING) and mixed point/polygon results are refused.

name: ST_WITHIN
description: Returns TRUE if no point of the first geography is outside the second and their interiors intersect; it is ST_CONTAINS with the arguments swapped.

name: ST_X
description: Returns the longitude in degrees of a single-point geography, and an error for any other geography.

name: ST_Y
description: Returns the latitude in degrees of a single-point geography, and an error for any other geography.

name: STARTS_WITH
description: Returns TRUE if a STRING or BYTES value begins with a given prefix, and FALSE otherwise.

name: STDDEV
description: Aggregate function that returns the sample standard deviation of the input values, ignoring NULLs; it is an alias for STDDEV_SAMP.

name: STDDEV_POP
description: Aggregate function that returns the population standard deviation of the input values, ignoring NULLs.

name: STDDEV_SAMP
description: Aggregate function that returns the sample (unbiased) standard deviation of the input values, ignoring NULLs.

name: STRING_AGG
description: Aggregate function that joins the non-NULL STRING or BYTES values of a group into one value, separated by a delimiter that is a comma by default.

name: STRPOS
description: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring or byte sequence inside a STRING or BYTES value, or 0 if it is not found.

name: STRUCT
description: Builds a struct value from a list of expressions, optionally with field names. As a type, STRUCT is an ordered collection of typed fields.

name: SUBSTR
description: Returns a substring of a STRING or BYTES value from a 1-based position, where a negative position counts back from the end, optionally limited to a length.

name: SUBSTR / SUBSTRING
description: SUBSTR and SUBSTRING are synonyms: each returns the part of a STRING or BYTES value that starts at a given position, with an optional length.

name: SUBSTRING
description: Alias for SUBSTR: returns the portion of a STRING or BYTES value that starts at a 1-based position, optionally limited to a given length.

name: SUM
description: Aggregate function that returns the sum of the non-NULL values in a group of rows.

name: TAN
description: Takes an angle given in radians and returns its tangent as a FLOAT64 value.

name: TANH
description: Takes a number and returns its hyperbolic tangent as a FLOAT64 value.

name: TEXT_ANALYZE
description: Extracts terms (tokens) from a STRING of text using a chosen analyzer and options, and returns them as an array of strings called a tokenized document.

name: TF_IDF
description: Analytic function that scores how relevant each term is to a tokenized document within a set of documents, returning an array of terms with their TF-IDF values.

name: TIME
description: As a function, creates a TIME value from hour, minute and second values or from a timestamp or datetime. As a type, TIME is a time of day with no date.

name: TIME_ADD
description: Adds a number of time units, such as hours, minutes or seconds, to a TIME value and returns the resulting TIME.

name: TIME_DIFF
description: Returns the number of unit boundaries, such as hours or minutes, between two TIME values.

name: TIME_SUB
description: Subtracts a number of time units, such as hours, minutes or seconds, from a TIME value and returns the resulting TIME.

name: TIME_TRUNC
description: Truncates a TIME value down to a chosen granularity, such as hour or minute, and returns the result as a TIME.

name: TIMESTAMP
description: As a function, converts a string, date or datetime to a TIMESTAMP, optionally using a time zone. As a type, TIMESTAMP is an absolute point in time.

name: TIMESTAMP_ADD
description: Adds a number of time units, from microseconds up to days, to a TIMESTAMP and returns the new TIMESTAMP, independent of any time zone.

name: TIMESTAMP_BUCKET
description: Returns the lower bound of the fixed-width bucket, set by an interval width and an optional origin, that contains a given timestamp.

name: TIMESTAMP_DIFF
description: Returns the number of unit boundaries, such as seconds, minutes or days, between two TIMESTAMP values, calculated as end minus start.

name: TIMESTAMP_MICROS
description: Interprets an INT64 as the number of microseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and returns the corresponding TIMESTAMP.

name: TIMESTAMP_MILLIS
description: Interprets an INT64 as the number of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and returns the corresponding TIMESTAMP.

name: TIMESTAMP_SECONDS
description: Interprets an INT64 as the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and returns the corresponding TIMESTAMP.

name: TIMESTAMP_SUB
description: Subtracts a number of time units, from microseconds up to days, from a TIMESTAMP and returns the new TIMESTAMP, independent of any time zone.

name: TIMESTAMP_TRUNC
description: Truncates a TIMESTAMP down to a chosen granularity, such as day, hour or month, optionally in a given time zone.

name: TO_BASE32
description: Converts a BYTES value into a base32-encoded STRING.

name: TO_BASE64
description: Converts a BYTES value into a base64-encoded STRING.

name: TO_CODE_POINTS
description: Converts a STRING into an array of INT64 Unicode code points, or a BYTES value into an array of extended ASCII byte values.

name: TO_HEX
description: Converts a BYTES value into a hexadecimal STRING, using two lowercase hexadecimal characters for each byte.

name: TO_JSON
description: Converts a SQL value of any type into a JSON value, with an option to represent very large numbers as strings.

name: TO_JSON_STRING
description: Converts a SQL value of any type into its JSON text form as a STRING, with an optional flag to pretty-print the output.

name: TO_JSON_STRING
description: Converts a SQL value of any type into its JSON text form as a STRING, with an optional flag to pretty-print the output.
notes: TO_JSON_STRING over an INTERVAL value is refused before execution (asserted).

name: TRANSLATE
description: Replaces each character of a source set that occurs in a STRING or BYTES value with the matching character of a target set.

name: TRIM
description: Removes leading and trailing characters, whitespace by default or a given set of characters, from a STRING or BYTES value.

name: TRUNC
description: Rounds a number toward zero, to a whole number or to a given number of decimal places.

name: TYPEOF
description: Returns the name of the data type of an expression as a STRING.

name: UNICODE
description: Returns the Unicode code point of the first character of a STRING as an INT64, or 0 if the string is empty.

name: UNIX_DATE
description: Returns the number of days between 1970-01-01 and a DATE value, as an INT64.

name: UNIX_MICROS
description: Returns the number of microseconds between 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and a TIMESTAMP value, as an INT64.

name: UNIX_MILLIS
description: Returns the number of milliseconds between 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and a TIMESTAMP value, as an INT64, rounding down any finer precision.

name: UNIX_SECONDS
description: Returns the number of seconds between 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and a TIMESTAMP value, as an INT64, rounding down any finer precision.

name: UPPER
description: Converts a STRING to uppercase using Unicode character rules, or a BYTES value to uppercase by treating it as ASCII text.

name: VAR_POP
description: Aggregate function that returns the population (biased) variance of the input values, ignoring NULLs.

name: VAR_SAMP
description: Aggregate function that returns the sample (unbiased) variance of the input values, ignoring NULLs.

name: VARIANCE
description: Aggregate function that returns the sample variance of the input values, ignoring NULLs; it is an alias for VAR_SAMP.

name: VARIANCE / VAR_POP / VAR_SAMP
description: Variance aggregate functions: VAR_POP returns the population variance, VAR_SAMP returns the sample variance, and VARIANCE is an alias for VAR_SAMP.
notes: NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC arguments are refused (only FLOAT64 overloads are registered); the DISTINCT modifier is refused; analytic calls over operands that can raise are refused.

name: VECTOR_INDEX.STATISTICS
description: Takes the name of a table that has a vector index and returns a FLOAT64 value showing how far the table data has drifted since the index was trained, to help decide when to rebuild it.

name: VECTOR_SEARCH
description: Table function that searches an embeddings column of a base table for the nearest matches to query embeddings and returns the matching rows with their distances.

name: WINDOW named specifications
description: Defines named windows in the WINDOW clause, each with partitioning, ordering and frame settings, that OVER clauses of window functions can refer to by name.

name: WITH
description: The WITH clause defines named temporary result sets that a query can reference. In graph queries, the WITH statement passes on chosen columns, optionally renamed or aggregated.

name: #legacySQL
description: A prefix on its own line before a query that makes BigQuery run it as legacy SQL, the older dialect, instead of GoogleSQL.

name: CROSS JOIN
description: Pairs every row of one input with every row of the other to produce the Cartesian product; it takes no ON or USING condition.

name: FULL OUTER JOIN
description: Returns all matching row pairs plus the rows from either input that have no match, filling the missing side's columns with NULL.

name: INNER JOIN
description: Returns only the pairs of rows that satisfy the join condition, so rows without a match on the other side are dropped.

name: LEFT JOIN
description: Shorthand for LEFT OUTER JOIN: keeps every row of the left input and fills the right input's columns with NULL when nothing matches.

name: LEFT [OUTER] JOIN
description: Returns all left-input rows joined to matching right-input rows, with NULLs for the right columns where there is no match; OUTER is optional.

name: ON clause
description: A join condition written as a boolean expression; a pair of rows is kept only when the expression evaluates to TRUE, and NULL counts as false.

name: RIGHT JOIN
description: Shorthand for RIGHT OUTER JOIN: keeps every row of the right input and fills the left input's columns with NULL when nothing matches.

name: RIGHT [OUTER] JOIN
description: Returns all right-input rows joined to matching left-input rows, with NULLs for the left columns where there is no match; OUTER is optional.

name: SELF JOIN
description: Joins a table to itself under two different aliases, for example to compare rows of the same table or to relate each employee to a manager.

name: USING
description: Join shorthand that lists column names present in both inputs and compares them for equality, instead of writing a full ON expression.

name: USING clause
description: Join condition of the form USING with a column list, where each named column must exist in both inputs; the listed columns come first in the output.

name: Array literals
description: Constant arrays written as a comma-separated list of elements in square brackets; the ARRAY keyword and an element type are optional, and [] is an empty array whose type is inferred.

name: BIGNUMERIC literals
description: A constant of the high-precision BIGNUMERIC type, written as the BIGNUMERIC keyword followed by a quoted number such as BIGNUMERIC '12'.

name: Case sensitivity
description: Rules for which parts of a query care about letter case: keywords, function names, column names and aliases do not, while string values, string comparisons and LIKE matching do.

name: Column names
description: The name of a column in a table, written as an unquoted or backtick-quoted identifier; quoting is needed when the name clashes with a reserved keyword.

name: Comments
description: Text the parser ignores: single-line comments start with a hash sign or two dashes, and multiline comments sit between a slash-asterisk and an asterisk-slash.

name: Date literals
description: A constant date written as the DATE keyword followed by a quoted year-month-day value such as DATE '2014-09-27'; years 1 through 9999 are valid.

name: Datetime literals
description: A constant calendar date with a time of day and no time zone, written as the DATETIME keyword and a quoted value such as DATETIME '2014-09-27 12:30:00.45'.

name: Escape sequences for string and bytes literals
description: Backslash codes allowed inside string and bytes literals, such as newline, tab, quote characters, octal and hex values and Unicode code points; any other sequence is an error.

name: Field names
description: The name of a field inside a STRUCT, protocol buffer message or JSON object, following the same rules as column names with quoted or unquoted identifiers.

name: Floating point literals
description: Numbers written with a decimal point or an exponent, such as 1.5 or 1e-3, which are floating point values; NaN and infinity have no literal and come from casting strings.

name: Formats for quoted literals
description: Ways to write string and bytes constants: single or double quotes, triple quotes for text spanning lines, an r prefix for raw text without escapes, and a b prefix for bytes.

name: Identifiers
description: Names given to columns, tables, fields and other objects; they can be unquoted or backtick-quoted, and a reserved keyword must be quoted to be used as a name.

name: Inline comments
description: A comment placed to the right of a statement on the same line, started by a hash sign or two dashes and running to the end of that line.

name: Integer literals
description: Whole numbers written as decimal digits or as hexadecimal with a 0x prefix, optionally with a leading sign; values in the 64-bit signed range are INT64.

name: Interval literal with a datetime part range
description: An INTERVAL constant written as a quoted string plus a starting and an ending datetime part, such as INTERVAL '10:20:30.52' HOUR TO SECOND.

name: Interval literal with a single datetime part
description: An INTERVAL constant made of an integer expression and one datetime part, such as INTERVAL 5 DAY or INTERVAL -5 DAY.

name: Interval literals
description: Constants of the INTERVAL type, written either as an integer with a single datetime part or as a quoted string with a range of parts; a negative sign distributes over the year and month parts or the time parts.

name: JSON literals
description: A constant of the JSON type, written as the JSON keyword followed by a quoted JSON text such as JSON '{"a": 1}'.

name: Literals
description: Constant values written directly in a query, such as strings, numbers, dates, arrays and structs; each has a built-in data type, though not every type has a literal form.

name: Multiline comments
description: A comment that can span several lines, enclosed between a slash-asterisk and an asterisk-slash; nested multiline comments are not allowed.

name: Named query parameters
description: Placeholders written as an at sign followed by a name, such as @myparam, whose values are bound outside the query text; they cannot be mixed with positional parameters.

name: NUMERIC literals
description: A constant of the exact decimal NUMERIC type, written as the NUMERIC keyword followed by a quoted number such as NUMERIC '12.34'.

name: Path expressions
description: A dotted sequence of names that navigates to an object, such as a table within a dataset or a field within a struct; a part that is a reserved keyword must be quoted if it comes first.

name: Positional query parameters
description: Placeholders written as a question mark, filled in by the order in which values are passed; they cannot be mixed with named parameters.

name: Query parameters
description: Placeholders in a query for values supplied separately at run time; they can stand in for expressions, but not for identifiers, column names or table names.

name: Quoted identifiers
description: Identifiers enclosed in backticks, which may contain spaces and symbols and let a reserved keyword be used as a name; they cannot be empty.

name: Range literals
description: A constant RANGE value written as a range type and a quoted pair of bounds, such as RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-12-31)'; a bound can be left open with UNBOUNDED.

name: Reserved keywords
description: Words with special meaning in the language, such as SELECT, FROM and WHERE, that cannot be used as identifiers unless enclosed in backticks; keywords are case-insensitive.

name: Single-line comments
description: A comment that occupies its own line, introduced by a hash sign, two dashes or a one-line slash-asterisk pair; the parser ignores it.

name: String and bytes literals
description: Constants of the STRING or BYTES type, written in single, double or triple quotes with a b prefix for bytes; adjacent literals separated by whitespace are joined into one.

name: Struct literals
description: A STRUCT whose fields are all literals, written with tuple syntax such as (1, 'abc'), as STRUCT(1 AS foo), or in typed form; tuple syntax needs at least two fields.

name: Table names
description: The name of a table, written as an unquoted or backtick-quoted identifier or as a multi-part path expression, following the language's case-sensitivity rules.

name: Terminating semicolons
description: A semicolon may end a statement; it is optional after the last statement but separates statements in a request that contains several.

name: Time literals
description: A constant time of day with no date or time zone, written as the TIME keyword followed by a quoted value such as TIME '12:30:00'.

name: Time zone
description: How a timestamp is tied to a time zone: given as a UTC offset such as '-08:00' or as a zone name such as America/Los_Angeles, with a default zone used when none is given.

name: Timestamp literals
description: A constant point in time written as the TIMESTAMP keyword and a quoted value, optionally with a UTC offset or zone name, such as TIMESTAMP '2014-09-27 12:30:00 America/Los_Angeles'.

name: Trailing commas
description: A comma is allowed after the last item of a SELECT column list, which makes it easier to generate column lists programmatically.

name: Unquoted identifiers
description: Identifiers written without quotes: they must begin with a letter or an underscore and may continue with letters, digits or underscores.

name: LIMIT with optional OFFSET
description: Caps how many rows a query returns and, with OFFSET, skips a number of leading rows first; row order is only predictable when ORDER BY is used.

name: ALL_DIFFERENT predicate
description: Graph predicate that takes a list of node or edge variables from a graph pattern and returns TRUE if no two of them are the same element, otherwise FALSE; a NULL element is an error.

name: Array subscript
description: Gets an element of an array by position using brackets: OFFSET counts from zero, ORDINAL from one, and the SAFE_ variants return NULL for a position out of range.

name: Concatenation
description: The operator that joins STRING values, BYTES values or arrays of the same element type end to end into one value; it is written with a double vertical bar.

name: Date arithmetics operators
description: Plus and minus operators that add or subtract a whole number of days to or from a DATE, giving a DATE, equivalent to DATE_ADD or DATE_SUB with a day interval.

name: Datetime subtraction
description: Subtracting one datetime value from another with the minus operator returns the difference as an INTERVAL value.

name: Field access
description: The dot operator, which gets a field from a STRUCT, protocol buffer, JSON value or graph element and can chain to reach nested fields, as in expression.field1.field2.

name: Graph logical operators
description: Operators that combine labels in a graph element pattern's label expression: NOT written with an exclamation mark, OR, and AND written with an ampersand.

name: Graph predicates
description: Graph-specific checks usable in graph expressions, such as PROPERTY_EXISTS, IS SOURCE, IS DESTINATION, IS LABELED and SAME, each producing TRUE, FALSE or NULL.

name: Interval arithmetic operators
description: Operators that add an INTERVAL to a datetime value or subtract one from it, and that multiply or divide an INTERVAL by an integer.

name: IS DESTINATION predicate
description: Graph predicate that checks whether a node is, or is not, the destination of an edge, taking a node variable and an edge variable and returning TRUE, FALSE or NULL.

name: IS DISTINCT FROM
description: Compares two values treating NULL as an ordinary value, so a NULL is distinct from any non-NULL but not from another NULL; the result is always TRUE or FALSE.

name: IS operators
description: Operators that test a condition and always return TRUE or FALSE, never NULL, such as IS NULL, IS TRUE, IS FALSE and IS UNKNOWN; adding NOT inverts the result.

name: IS SOURCE predicate
description: Graph predicate that checks whether a node is, or is not, the source of an edge, taking a node variable and an edge variable and returning TRUE, FALSE or NULL.

name: JSON subscript
description: Reads an array element by zero-based index or an object field by name from a JSON value using brackets; a missing index or field yields NULL.

name: LIKE
description: Returns TRUE when the first operand matches the pattern in the second; NOT LIKE returns TRUE when it does not, and a backslash can escape the percent and underscore wildcards.

name: Logical operators
description: AND, OR and NOT, which accept only BOOL or NULL operands and follow three-valued logic; the order in which AND and OR evaluate their operands is not fixed.

name: Operator list
description: Summary table naming each operator in the language, such as field access, subscripts, arithmetic, comparison and logical operators, with a one-line description of each.

name: Operator precedence
description: Table ranking the operators from highest to lowest precedence, which decides the order they are evaluated in an expression that has no parentheses.

name: Quantified LIKE
description: Checks a STRING or BYTES value against several patterns at once using LIKE ANY, LIKE SOME or LIKE ALL, with the patterns given as a list, an array or a subquery.

name: SAME predicate
description: Graph predicate that checks whether all the node or edge variables in a list are bound to the same graph element, returning TRUE or FALSE; a NULL element is an error.

name: Struct subscript
description: Gets a field of a STRUCT by its position instead of its name, using brackets with OFFSET or ORDINAL; the SAFE_ variants return NULL for an out-of-range position.

name: WITH expression
description: Creates one or more named variables inside an expression, each able to use the ones before it, and returns the value of a final result expression.

name: SAMPLE
description: Takes a random subset of a table's rows with TABLESAMPLE, useful for exploring or approximating answers over very large tables.

name: TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (n PERCENT)
description: Returns a random sample of roughly the stated percentage of a table, between 0 and 100, and the rows chosen can differ from run to run.
A positional query parameter placeholder; values are bound in order of appearance, and positional and named parameters cannot be mixed in one query.
notes: RANGE parameters are refused; TIMESTAMP values with a named time zone other than UTC or Etc/UTC are refused.

name: @param
description: A named query parameter written as @ followed by a name, whose typed value is supplied separately from the SQL text; it cannot stand in for identifiers or table names.
notes: RANGE parameters are refused; TIMESTAMP values with a named time zone other than UTC or Etc/UTC are refused.

name: Pipe-first query style
description: Writes a query as a starting table followed by a chain of pipe operators, so each step reads in the order it runs instead of nesting clauses.

name: |> SELECT, |> WHERE, |> AGGREGATE, |> ORDER BY, etc.
description: Pipe operators such as SELECT, WHERE, AGGREGATE and ORDER BY, each taking the table produced by the previous step and returning a new table.

name: AGGREGATE pipe
description: Pipe operator that summarizes the input table with aggregate functions, giving one row for the whole table or one row per group when GROUP BY is attached; grouping columns come first.

name: Aggregation function in the HAVING clause.
description: Rule that the aggregate function may sit in the HAVING condition itself, as in HAVING SUM(points) > 15, so groups can be filtered on a value that is not in the SELECT list.

name: Aggregation function in the SELECT list.
description: Rule that the aggregate function may instead be in the SELECT list, where HAVING can filter on its alias, as in SELECT SUM(x) AS total with HAVING total > 15.

name: Aggregation in both the SELECT list and HAVING clause.
description: Rule that aggregates may appear in both the SELECT list and the HAVING clause, and they do not need to be the same function or use the same columns.

name: AGGREGATION_THRESHOLD clause
description: Clause that counts distinct privacy units per group using a privacy unit column and returns only groups whose count reaches a given threshold, omitting smaller groups.

name: Aliases (AS)
description: Gives a table, column or expression a temporary name with AS, which is optional; the alias can then be used elsewhere in the query within the visibility rules.

name: Array subqueries
description: Subquery written ARRAY(subquery) that returns the rows of a single-column query as an array, an empty array for no rows and never NULL; with SELECT AS STRUCT it builds arrays of structs.

name: ARRAY subquery
description: Subquery expression that turns the rows of a query into an array, giving an empty array for no rows and never NULL; written ARRAY(subquery) in SQL and ARRAY with braces around a graph query.
notes: An ARRAY subquery with a volatile element (ARRAY(SELECT RAND())) is refused; an aggregate inside a correlated ARRAY source (ARRAY(SELECT SUM(x) FROM UNNEST(a) x)) is refused; a correlated ARRAY source whose WHERE can raise an error is refused; computed NUMERIC elements (ARRAY(SELECT x * NUMERIC '2' ...)) are refused; an ARRAY subquery over an error-capable outer source column is refused.

name: AS pipe
description: Pipe operator that gives the current table a new alias, replacing existing table aliases, so later operators such as JOIN can qualify its columns.

name: Basic SELECT
description: The core query form: SELECT a list of columns or expressions FROM a table, returning one output row per input row unless rows are filtered or grouped.

name: CALL pipe
description: Pipe operator that calls a table-valued function, passing the pipe input table as its first table argument unless INPUT TABLE marks a different argument.

name: Changing from the default dialect
description: How to choose between GoogleSQL and legacy SQL for a query: through query settings, a dialect prefix at the start of the query, or the use_legacy_sql flag of the bq tool.

name: COLLATE
description: Applies a collation to STRING values: in ORDER BY it controls how values sort, and the COLLATE function returns a string that carries a given collation.

name: Comma cross join (,)
description: Writes a CROSS JOIN as a comma between two FROM items, pairing every row of the first item with every row of the second.

name: Correlated join operation
description: A join where the right FROM item refers to the left one, such as an array column, so the right rows depend on each left row; RIGHT and FULL OUTER joins cannot be correlated.

name: Correlated subqueries
description: Subqueries that refer to columns of the outer query, so they must logically be evaluated again for each distinct set of outer values.

name: cte_name
description: The name given to a common table expression in a WITH clause, which the query can then use in FROM like a table; it hides a permanent table of the same name.

name: CTE rules and constraints
description: Rules for CTEs: names in one WITH clause must be unique, RECURSIVE is required for self-reference, a local CTE overrides an outer name, and recursive CTEs have base and recursive term limits.

name: CTE visibility
description: Which CTEs in a WITH clause can see which others: without RECURSIVE a CTE sees only those defined before it, with RECURSIVE references may go either way but cycles are not allowed.

name: DEFINE clause
description: In MATCH_RECOGNIZE, defines each pattern symbol with a boolean condition; a row matches the symbol when the condition is TRUE, and every symbol must appear in the PATTERN.

name: delta
description: Differential privacy parameter for the probability that a result row fails to be epsilon-differentially private; setting it very close to 1 keeps small groups but removes protection.

name: DISTINCT pipe
description: Pipe operator that returns the distinct rows of the input table, comparing all visible columns, while keeping table aliases so later operators can still use them.

name: epsilon
description: Differential privacy parameter that controls how much noise is added to the results; a higher epsilon means less noise and weaker privacy protection.

name: EXCEPT
description: Set operator that returns rows of the left query that are not present in the right query; ALL or DISTINCT controls how duplicate rows are treated.

name: EXCEPT pipe
description: Pipe form of EXCEPT: returns rows of the input table that are absent from every query listed in parentheses after the operator, so several queries can be subtracted in one step.

name: EXISTS / NOT EXISTS
description: Checks whether a subquery returns at least one row, giving TRUE or FALSE and never NULL; NOT EXISTS reverses it, which is a common way to find rows with no match.
notes: EXISTS over a volatile select list (EXISTS(SELECT RAND())) is refused; EXISTS inside an untaken conditional branch whose subquery can raise (IF(FALSE, EXISTS(SELECT DIV(1,0)), TRUE)) is refused instead of returning TRUE; EXISTS correlated to an outer column computed by an error-capable expression is refused instead of evaluated.

name: EXISTS subqueries
description: Expression subquery written EXISTS(subquery) that is TRUE when the subquery produces one or more rows and FALSE for none, whatever columns it selects.

name: Explicit and implicit UNNEST
description: Two ways to flatten an array in FROM: explicit unnesting uses the UNNEST keyword, while implicit unnesting omits it and names an array path that starts with a table alias.

name: Expression subqueries
description: Subqueries used wherever an expression is valid that return a single value: scalar, ARRAY, IN, EXISTS and quantified LIKE forms; they can be correlated.

name: EXTEND pipe
description: Pipe operator that keeps all existing columns and appends new computed columns, like SELECT star plus extra expressions; it can use window functions.

name: field_path
description: In FROM, a path that resolves to an array or repeated field inside another column, such as t1.array_column, which is flattened into rows; it cannot pass through another array before its end.

name: FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF
description: Reads a table as it was at a past timestamp, given as a constant expression that cannot be in the future or more than seven days before the current time.

name: FROM clause
description: Names the tables, subqueries, joins, UNNEST operations and other sources a query reads from, and how they are combined into one stream of rows for the rest of the query.

name: FROM queries
description: In pipe syntax, a query may begin with a FROM clause alone, which returns all rows of the source, with pipe operators optionally added after it.

name: GRAPH_EXPAND
description: Table-valued function that takes a property graph and returns a relational table of its node and edge data, with columns flattened by default.

name: graph_table_operator
description: In FROM, the GRAPH_TABLE operator runs a graph query over a property graph and returns the result as a table, with an optional alias for that table.

name: GROUP BY clause
description: Groups rows with the same values in the listed expressions into single rows so aggregate functions summarize each group; it accepts values, ordinals, ALL, GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP and CUBE.

name: Group rows by ALL
description: GROUP BY ALL infers the grouping keys from the SELECT list, leaving out aggregate expressions, window expressions and constants; if no keys remain, all rows form one group.

name: Group rows by column ordinals
description: Lets GROUP BY refer to SELECT list items by position, where 1 is the first item, 2 the second and so on; ordinals can be mixed with names.

name: Group rows by CUBE
description: GROUP BY CUBE produces aggregated rows for every combination of the listed grouping items, which helps build contingency tables showing how items relate.

name: Group rows by groupable items
description: The basic GROUP BY list: groupable expressions with optional aliases, or their ordinals, where rows with equal values fall into the same group.

name: Group rows by GROUPING SETS
description: GROUP BY GROUPING SETS produces aggregates for each listed grouping set, a set of columns to group by, giving several levels of summary in one result.

name: Group rows by ROLLUP
description: GROUP BY ROLLUP produces aggregates for each leading prefix of the listed items, which suits rolling up subtotals and a grand total.

name: Group rows by values
description: Groups rows that share equal values in the GROUP BY expressions, as in GROUP BY LastName with SUM(PointsScored) giving one total per last name.

name: HAVING clause
description: Filters the rows produced by GROUP BY or aggregation, keeping those where the condition is TRUE; it can use SELECT aliases and needs aggregation to be present.

name: IN subqueries
description: Subquery form value IN (subquery), which is TRUE if the value appears among the rows of a single-column subquery and FALSE if the subquery returns no rows.

name: IN subquery
description: Checks whether a value is in the result of a subquery that returns one comparable column; NOT IN reverses it, and graph queries use the same test with a graph query in braces.
notes: An IN subquery with a volatile select list (1.0 IN (SELECT RAND())) is refused; STRUCT operands (STRUCT(1 AS x) IN (SELECT STRUCT(1 AS x))) are refused.

name: INTERSECT
description: Set operator that returns the rows found in the results of both the left and right queries; ALL or DISTINCT controls how duplicate rows are handled.

name: INTERSECT pipe
description: Pipe form of INTERSECT: returns rows that appear in the input table and in every query listed in parentheses after the operator.

name: Join conditions
description: The ON or USING clause that decides which pairs of rows from the two FROM items stay in the join output; CROSS JOIN takes no condition.

name: Join operation
description: Combines two FROM items by pairing their rows and filtering with a condition; the kinds are INNER, CROSS, FULL, LEFT and RIGHT joins, plus LATERAL references.

name: Join operations in a sequence
description: A FROM clause may chain several JOINs, which bind from left to right; parentheses regroup them so a later join is evaluated first.

name: JOIN pipe
description: Pipe operator that joins the input table, as the left side, with a table, subquery, UNNEST or table function given as its argument; LEFT, INNER and CROSS can precede JOIN.

name: LIMIT and OFFSET clause
description: LIMIT caps the number of rows produced, with LIMIT 0 returning none, and OFFSET skips rows before the limit applies; use them after ORDER BY for a repeatable choice of rows.

name: LIMIT pipe
description: Pipe operator that caps the number of rows from the input table, with an optional OFFSET to skip rows first; it keeps the order of an ordered input.

name: Limit the groups in which a privacy unit ID can exist
description: Shows how max_groups_contributed in a differentially private query bounds how many groups each privacy unit can appear in, which also scales the noise.

name: MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause
description: Finds matches of a row pattern, like a regular expression over ordered rows, optionally within partitions, and returns MEASURES values computed for each match.

name: MATCH_RECOGNIZE pipe
description: Pipe form of MATCH_RECOGNIZE: searches the input table for ordered row sequences that fit a pattern and returns values computed for each match.

name: max_groups_contributed
description: Differential privacy parameter, a positive integer, that limits how many groups one privacy unit may contribute to and scales the noise added to each group.

name: MEASURES clause
description: In MATCH_RECOGNIZE, lists the aliased aggregate expressions computed for each match; symbol.column limits an aggregation to rows matched by that symbol.

name: MEASURES clause functions
description: Functions for MEASURES in MATCH_RECOGNIZE: FIRST and LAST return a value from a match's first or last row, MATCH_NUMBER numbers matches, and CLASSIFIER and MATCH_ROW_NUMBER describe rows.

name: ON and USING equivalency
description: Compares the two join conditions: ON keeps both key columns while USING returns one merged column, and NULL keys never match under either, so results can differ.

name: ORDER BY clause
description: Sorts the result by one or more expressions, ascending or descending, with optional COLLATE and NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST; without it the row order is undefined.

name: ORDER BY pipe
description: Pipe operator that sorts the input table by a list of expressions, with the same ASC, DESC and NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST options as the ORDER BY clause.

name: Order preservation
description: Pipe rule: SELECT, EXTEND, SET, DROP, RENAME, AS, LIMIT and WITH keep an ordered input in order, so a LIMIT after them takes the top rows by that order.

name: Order-sensitive aggregate functions
description: Rule in MATCH_RECOGNIZE measures: functions such as ARRAY_AGG and STRING_AGG read their input in the clause's ORDER BY order unless DISTINCT or an explicit ordering is given.

name: Parameterized queries (@param)
description: Queries that use named placeholders such as @name, with the values supplied separately from the SQL text, so one query text can be reused with different values.

name: PARTITION BY clause
description: In MATCH_RECOGNIZE, splits the input rows into partitions and looks for matches only inside each partition; without it the whole table is a single partition.

name: PATTERN clause
description: In MATCH_RECOGNIZE, defines what a match looks like as a regular-expression-like sequence of the symbols named in DEFINE, with grouping, alternation, anchors and quantifiers.

name: Pipe
description: Query syntax in which operators are chained with the pipe symbol, each taking the previous result table and producing a new one; it can start from FROM and mix with standard syntax.

name: Pipe operator list
description: Reference table of the pipe operators, from SELECT, EXTEND, WHERE and AGGREGATE through JOIN, UNION and PIVOT to MATCH_RECOGNIZE, each with a one-line summary.

name: Pipe operator semantics
description: Rules for how pipe operators behave: each performs one self-contained operation, consumes its input table to produce a new table, and sees only columns of that immediate input.

name: Pipe operators
description: The operators used after the pipe symbol to transform a table step by step, such as filtering, aggregating, joining, sorting and limiting, each with its own syntax.

name: PIVOT
description: FROM-clause operator that rotates rows into columns by aggregating values for each listed pivot value, so values of one column become new column names.

name: pivot_operator
description: The PIVOT syntax element in FROM: aggregate function calls, a FOR column with an IN list of values, optional prefixes, and an optional alias for the result.

name: PIVOT pipe
description: Pipe operator that rotates rows of the input table into columns, one new column per listed value, with optional aliases for pivot columns and for the result table.

name: privacy_unit_column
description: Differential privacy option naming the column that identifies the privacy unit, the entity whose data is protected, so each unit's contribution can be bounded.

name: QUALIFY
description: Filters rows after window functions have been computed, keeping those whose condition is TRUE; a window function must appear in the QUALIFY condition or the SELECT list.

name: QUALIFY clause
description: The clause evaluated after HAVING and WINDOW, which lets a query filter on window function results directly without wrapping it in a subquery.

name: query_expr
description: A full query, including SELECT, set operations and WITH, that can appear in parentheses as a table subquery in FROM, optionally followed by an alias.

name: Range variables
description: A table alias in FROM that stands for the rows scanned from a table expression and qualifies columns, as in alias.column; for a value table it refers to the whole row value.

name: Recursive CTE
description: A CTE defined by a base term and a recursive term joined with UNION ALL, where the recursive term refers to the CTE itself and repeats until it produces no rows.

name: Recursive CTEs
description: CTEs that reference themselves: the base term runs first, then the recursive term repeatedly consumes the previous iteration's rows; the WITH clause must include RECURSIVE.

name: RECURSIVE keyword
description: Keyword on WITH that allows self-referencing CTEs and also lets any CTE in the clause be referenced by any other, regardless of the order they are written in.

name: RENAME pipe
description: Pipe operator that renames the listed columns of the input table and leaves the others unchanged; each column to rename must exist exactly once.

name: RETURN
description: In a graph query, ends a linear query statement and returns the result columns, with optional grouping, ordering and limits. In a script, stops execution of the script.

name: Return query results as a value table
description: Uses SELECT AS STRUCT, SELECT AS VALUE or SELECT AS with a type name so that each result row is a single value instead of a list of columns.

name: Scalar subqueries
description: A parenthesized subquery that selects one column and is used as a value: it gives that value for one row, NULL for no rows, and a runtime error for more than one row.

name: SELECT
description: Defines the output columns of a query as a list of columns or expressions with optional aliases, evaluated over the rows left after FROM, filtering and grouping.

name: SELECT ALL
description: Returns all rows including duplicates; this is the default behavior of SELECT, so ALL only makes it explicit.

name: SELECT AS STRUCT
description: Returns each row as one STRUCT whose fields are the selected columns, producing a value table; often used in subqueries to return several values as a single struct.

name: SELECT AS STRUCT / SELECT AS VALUE
description: Output modifiers that produce a value table: AS STRUCT packs the selected columns into a struct per row, while AS VALUE takes exactly one column and returns its value as the whole row.

name: SELECT AS VALUE
description: Produces a value table from a SELECT list with exactly one column, discarding its name so each row is just that value, such as a struct, instead of a one-column table.

name: SELECT DISTINCT
description: Removes duplicate rows from the result, keeping one copy of each distinct combination of selected values.

name: SELECT DISTINCT / SELECT APPROXDISTINCT
description: Eliminates duplicate rows so every distinct combination of the selected values is returned only once.

name: SELECT * EXCEPT
description: Returns every column except the named ones, for example SELECT * EXCEPT (order_id); columns that have no name are not excluded.

name: SELECT expression
description: A SELECT list item that evaluates an expression into one output column with an optional alias; without an explicit alias it may get an implicit one, otherwise it is anonymous.

name: SELECT pipe
description: Pipe operator that produces a new table containing only the listed columns or expressions; it allows DISTINCT, AS STRUCT and window functions but does not aggregate.

name: SELECT * REPLACE
description: Returns all columns but replaces the value of named columns with new expressions, as in SELECT * REPLACE (quantity/2 AS quantity); names and column order stay the same.

name: Set operators
description: The UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT operators, which combine the results of two queries into one, matching columns by position or by name, with ALL or DISTINCT for duplicates.

name: SET pipe
description: Pipe operator that replaces the values of existing columns with new expressions, like SELECT * REPLACE; each named column must exist exactly once in the input.

name: Shorthand ordering syntax with AGGREGATE
description: In AGGREGATE, GROUP AND ORDER BY or ASC and DESC suffixes on group or aggregate items sort the output without a separate ORDER BY operator.

name: Subqueries (scalar / table)
description: A query nested inside another: a scalar subquery gives a single value inside an expression, and a table subquery supplies rows in the FROM clause under an alias.
notes: A scalar subquery that returns a STRUCT under LIMIT is refused (SELECT (SELECT STRUCT(1) LIMIT 1)).

name: Table function calls
description: Calling a table-valued function in FROM in place of a table name, passing a table argument either as a subquery or as TABLE followed by a table name.

name: table_name
description: The name of an existing table in FROM, optionally qualified as in db.Roster and optionally followed by an alias.

name: Table subqueries
description: A parenthesized query in FROM that the outer query treats as a table, optionally with an alias; this kind of subquery is only allowed in the FROM clause.

name: TABLESAMPLE
description: FROM-clause operator that returns a random sample of a table, such as TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10 PERCENT); each run might return different rows, so it suits approximate queries on large tables.

name: tablesample_operator
description: The TABLESAMPLE syntax element in FROM that follows a table and states the sampling method and the sample size, so the query reads only a random subset.

name: TABLESAMPLE pipe
description: Pipe operator that returns a random sample of the input table, for example about one percent of a large table, behaving like the TABLESAMPLE operator.

name: UNION
description: Set operator that stacks the rows of the left and right queries, matching columns by position; UNION ALL keeps duplicates and UNION DISTINCT removes them.

name: UNION pipe
description: Pipe form of UNION: appends the rows of one or more comma-separated parenthesized queries to the input table, with the same ALL, DISTINCT and BY NAME modifiers.

name: UNNEST and NULL values
description: UNNEST of a NULL array or an empty array produces zero rows, while an array containing NULL elements produces a row holding NULL for each of them.

name: UNNEST and structs
description: Unnesting an array of structs gives one row per struct with a column for each struct field, named after the field; giving the UNNEST an alias lets you select the whole struct.

name: unnest_operator
description: The UNNEST syntax element in FROM: an array expression with an optional alias, and optional WITH OFFSET to add an index column, producing one row per element.

name: UNPIVOT
description: FROM-clause operator that rotates columns into rows as name and value pairs; rows with NULL values are left out unless INCLUDE NULLS is given.

name: unpivot_operator
description: The UNPIVOT syntax element in FROM: optional INCLUDE or EXCLUDE NULLS, a values column, a FOR name column, an IN list of source columns, and an optional alias.

name: UNPIVOT pipe
description: Pipe operator that rotates columns of the input table into rows, behaving like the UNPIVOT operator in standard syntax.

name: Use a set operation on a value table
description: UNION ALL and other set operations can combine value tables with each other or with a one-column table of the matching type, and the result is always a value table.

name: Value tables
description: Tables whose rows are single values, such as a STRUCT, with no column names; they come from SELECT AS VALUE, SELECT AS STRUCT or UNNEST of an array.

name: Visibility in the FROM clause
description: Aliases in FROM are processed from left to right and are visible only to later items, so an item can refer to an alias introduced before it, such as an array column of a preceding table.

name: Visibility in the GROUP BY, ORDER BY, and HAVING clauses
description: GROUP BY, ORDER BY and HAVING can refer to tables in FROM and their columns and to SELECT list aliases; GROUP BY and ORDER BY can also use integer ordinals pointing at SELECT list items.

name: Visibility in the SELECT list
description: Aliases defined in the SELECT list are visible only to the GROUP BY, ORDER BY and HAVING clauses, not to other expressions in the same SELECT list.

name: Visibility of CTEs in a WITH clause with the RECURSIVE keyword
description: With RECURSIVE, CTEs may refer to themselves and to each other, forwards or backwards, as long as there are no cycles such as A referencing B referencing A.

name: Visibility of CTEs in a WITH clause without the RECURSIVE keyword
description: Without RECURSIVE, a CTE can refer only to CTEs defined before it in the WITH clause; self-references and forward references are errors.

name: WHERE clause
description: Filters the rows from FROM before grouping, keeping only rows whose condition is TRUE; rows that evaluate to FALSE or NULL are discarded.

name: WHERE pipe
description: Pipe operator that filters the input table like the WHERE clause and also takes the place of HAVING and QUALIFY, for example after AGGREGATE or on window function results.

name: WINDOW clause
description: Defines named windows, each a partition and ordering specification, that window functions can reuse by name in OVER; a named window may build on one defined earlier.

name: WITH clause
description: Defines one or more CTEs, named subquery results that the rest of the query can use like temporary tables; the clause can hold recursive and non-recursive CTEs.

name: WITH (CTE)
description: Starts a query with named subqueries, called common table expressions, that the main SELECT can reference by name instead of repeating or nesting them.

name: WITH DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY
description: SELECT modifier that makes aggregates differentially private, adding noise controlled by options such as epsilon, delta and max_groups_contributed, with a privacy unit.

name: WITH OFFSET
description: Optional part of UNNEST that adds a column with each element's zero-based position in the array; the column is named offset unless an alias is given.

name: WITH pipe
description: Pipe operator that defines CTEs for the rest of the query while passing its input table through unchanged; recursive CTEs and a trailing comma are allowed.

name: ASSERT
description: Evaluates a boolean expression and stops the script with an error if it is not TRUE; an optional AS message is reported with the error.

name: BEGIN...EXCEPTION...END
description: A block whose EXCEPTION clause acts as an error handler for the statements before it, letting a script recover from failures or run cleanup such as a rollback.

name: CALL
description: Invokes a stored procedure by name with an argument list; OUT and INOUT arguments must be variables of the matching type.

name: CASE
description: As an expression, returns the result of the first WHEN condition that is TRUE, else the ELSE result or NULL; as a scripting statement, runs the statements of the first matching WHEN branch.

name: FOR...IN
description: Loops over every row returned by a query, assigning each row to a loop variable that is a STRUCT of the row's top-level columns.

name: IF
description: As a function, IF returns one of two values depending on a condition; as a scripting statement, IF runs the first block of statements whose condition is true, with optional ELSEIF and ELSE blocks.

name: LOOP
description: Repeats a list of statements indefinitely until a BREAK or LEAVE statement exits the loop.

name: SET
description: Assigns the value of an expression to a variable, or to several variables at once, within a multi-statement query.

name: WHILE
description: Repeats a list of statements as long as a boolean condition is TRUE, evaluating the condition before each pass.

name: BEGIN / END
description: Groups statements into a block; variables declared inside exist only until the matching END and cannot be referenced outside the block.

name: BEGIN / EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN / END
description: Error-handling form of a block: statements run in order, and if one fails the remainder is skipped and the statements after EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN run instead.
notes: @@error.stack_trace and @@error.formatted_stack_trace are not available.

name: BEGIN TRANSACTION
description: Starts a multi-statement transaction that ends at COMMIT TRANSACTION or ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; if the script ends first, the changes are rolled back.

name: BREAK
description: Exits the current loop immediately and continues with the statement after the loop; it is an error to use it outside a loop.

name: CALL procedure()
description: A call that names a stored procedure followed by parentheses holding its arguments, running the procedure body as part of the script.
notes: Procedures in another project are refused; argument types outside the admitted script-variable types (for example JSON, GEOGRAPHY, INTERVAL, RANGE, nested STRUCT) are refused; a procedure called from outside its own dataset refuses body statements whose table, view, model or function names lack a dataset.

name: COMMIT
description: Makes the changes of the open transaction permanent and ends it; the statement fails if no transaction is open.
notes: COMMIT in an exception handler after a runtime error inside the transaction is refused and the script fails with the transaction rolled back, whereas BigQuery commits the work done before the error.

name: CONTINUE
description: Skips the remaining statements of the current loop iteration and returns to the start of the loop; it is an error outside a loop.

name: CREATE PROCEDURE ... BEGIN ... END
description: Defines a stored procedure whose body is a BEGIN and END block of statements, which can later be run with CALL.
notes: Argument types outside the admitted script-variable types (for example JSON, GEOGRAPHY, INTERVAL, RANGE, nested STRUCT) are refused; procedures in another project are refused; procedures cannot be created through REST routines.insert.

name: DECLARE
description: Declares a script variable with an optional type and DEFAULT value; without a default it starts as NULL, and the type can be inferred from the default.

name: ELSEIF
description: An additional condition inside IF that is checked when the earlier conditions are not TRUE, running its statement list if it is.

name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
description: Runs a SQL string built at runtime as a statement, optionally storing results INTO variables and binding values through a USING list.

name: FOR / IN / DO / END FOR
description: Full loop form where each row of the query after IN is bound to the loop variable and the statements between DO and END FOR run once per row.
notes: The query's columns must be distinct and named, and each must fit a STRUCT field type admitted for script variables (INT64, STRING, BYTES, BOOL, DATE, TIME, FLOAT64), so queries returning TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC, ARRAY, STRUCT, JSON, GEOGRAPHY or INTERVAL columns, or anonymous columns, are refused; a loop variable named like a visible variable is refused.

name: IF / THEN / ELSE / END IF
description: Conditional form that runs the statements after THEN when the condition is TRUE, otherwise the optional ELSE statements, and is closed by END IF.

name: Labels on blocks
description: A name placed before BEGIN, LOOP, WHILE, FOR or REPEAT so that BREAK, LEAVE, CONTINUE or ITERATE can name the exact block or loop to exit or restart.

name: LEAVE / ITERATE
description: LEAVE is another name for BREAK and exits the loop; ITERATE is another name for CONTINUE and jumps to the next iteration.

name: LOOP / END LOOP
description: The full form of the unconditional loop, where the statements between LOOP and END LOOP repeat until one of them executes BREAK or LEAVE.

name: @@project_id
description: A read-only system variable holding the ID of the project that runs the current query; inside a procedure it is the project running the script, not the one owning the procedure.
notes: @@project_id is declared to the analyzer only inside multi-statement queries, procedures and sessions with variables, so a standalone single-statement query that reads it fails with an analyzer error.

name: RAISE USING MESSAGE
description: Raises an error with a custom message text; without USING MESSAGE it re-raises the caught error and is only allowed inside an EXCEPTION clause.

name: REPEAT / UNTIL / END REPEAT
description: Runs the statements first and then checks the UNTIL condition, repeating the loop until that condition becomes TRUE.

name: ROLLBACK
description: Undoes all changes made since the transaction began and ends it; the statement fails if no transaction is open.

name: @@row_count
description: A read-only system variable that gives the number of rows affected by the previous DML statement in a multi-statement query.
notes: @@row_count is declared to the analyzer only inside multi-statement queries, procedures and sessions with variables, so a standalone single-statement query that reads it fails with an analyzer error instead of returning NULL.

name: SET variable
description: Sets a declared script variable to the value of an expression, or assigns several variables together using parenthesized lists.

name: Variable references
description: Uses a declared script variable by name inside expressions, queries and later statements, within the block where it was declared.

name: WHILE / DO / END WHILE
description: Loop form where the condition is checked before every pass and the statements between DO and END WHILE run while it stays TRUE.

name: CALL procedure_name(args);
description: Statement that runs a stored procedure, passing arguments by position, so reusable SQL logic can be invoked from a script.
notes: Procedures in another project are refused; argument types outside the admitted script-variable types (for example JSON, GEOGRAPHY, INTERVAL, RANGE, nested STRUCT) are refused; a procedure called from outside its own dataset refuses body statements whose table, view, model or function names lack a dataset.

name: COMMIT TRANSACTION;
description: Ends the open multi-statement transaction and makes all of its changes permanent, failing if no transaction is open.
notes: COMMIT in an exception handler after a runtime error inside the transaction is refused and the script fails with the transaction rolled back, whereas BigQuery commits the work done before the error.

name: DECLARE var_name [TYPE] [DEFAULT value];
description: Creates a variable in a script, where the type can be left out when a DEFAULT expression lets BigQuery infer it; several names can share one declaration.
notes: Variable types are limited to INT64, FLOAT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, DATE, TIME, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC, STRUCTs whose fields are INT64, STRING, BYTES, BOOL, DATE, TIME or FLOAT64, and ARRAYs of those scalars (not TIMESTAMP or DATETIME) or STRUCTs, so JSON, GEOGRAPHY, INTERVAL, RANGE, nested STRUCT and ARRAY<TIMESTAMP> variables are refused; parameterized types such as STRING(10) are refused.

name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE sql_string [INTO vars] [USING params];
description: Executes a dynamically built SQL string; INTO captures a returned row into variables and USING binds values to placeholders in the string.
notes: USING values and INTO targets are limited to the admitted script-variable types, so JSON, GEOGRAPHY, INTERVAL, RANGE and nested composite values are refused.

name: FOR variable IN (query) DO ... END FOR;
description: Iterates over a query result one row at a time, with the loop variable giving field access to each row's columns inside the loop body.
notes: The query's columns must be distinct and named, and each must fit a STRUCT field type admitted for script variables (INT64, STRING, BYTES, BOOL, DATE, TIME, FLOAT64), so queries returning TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC, ARRAY, STRUCT, JSON, GEOGRAPHY or INTERVAL columns, or anonymous columns, are refused; a loop variable named like a visible variable is refused.

name: IF condition THEN ... [ELSEIF ...] [ELSE ...] END IF;
description: Runs the first statement list whose condition is TRUE among the IF, any ELSEIF and the final ELSE parts, and then continues after END IF.

name: ITERATE;
description: Skips the rest of the current loop pass and starts the next iteration; it is the same statement as CONTINUE.

name: LEAVE;
description: Exits the current loop or labeled block immediately; it is the same statement as BREAK.

name: Multi-statement scripts (anonymous)
description: A series of statements separated by semicolons that BigQuery runs as a single script job, in order, without needing to be wrapped in a stored procedure.
notes: Child jobs are recorded only for scripts without expression evaluation (no DECLARE, SET, IF, loops or handlers), and jobs.list parentJobId is refused for the others; scriptStatistics, @@script.* and @@current_job_id are absent; SET of system variables (such as @@time_zone or @@dataset_id) and system variables other than @@row_count, @@project_id and @@error.message/statement_text are refused.

name: RAISE
description: Raises an error in a script, stopping execution unless a surrounding EXCEPTION clause handles it; on its own inside a handler it re-raises the caught error.

name: REPEAT ... UNTIL condition END REPEAT;
description: Do-until style loop: the body executes at least once and repeats until the condition after UNTIL is TRUE.

name: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
description: Cancels the open multi-statement transaction and discards its changes; often used inside an exception handler after an error.

name: SET var_name = expression;
description: Evaluates an expression and stores the result in an already declared variable, replacing its previous value.

name: WHILE condition DO ... END WHILE;
description: Repeats the loop body as long as the condition evaluates to TRUE, checking it before each iteration so the body may never run.

name: EXCEPT {ALL | DISTINCT}
description: Returns rows from the left query that are absent from the right query, written with either ALL, which keeps remaining duplicates, or DISTINCT, which returns each row once.
notes: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused; BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: INTERSECT {ALL | DISTINCT}
description: Returns rows found in both input queries, written with either ALL, which keeps duplicates up to their count in both inputs, or DISTINCT, which returns each shared row once.
notes: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused; BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: UNION {ALL | DISTINCT}
description: Combines the rows of two queries into one result, written with either ALL, which keeps every row, or DISTINCT, which removes duplicate rows.
notes: BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered); UNION DISTINCT: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused.

name: EXCEPT DISTINCT
description: Returns each distinct row of the left query that does not appear in the right query, with duplicates removed from the result.
notes: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused; BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: INTERSECT DISTINCT
description: Returns each distinct row that appears in both queries, listing it once no matter how many times it occurs.
notes: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused; BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: UNION ALL
description: Appends the rows of the second query to those of the first, keeping every row including duplicates; columns are matched by position.
notes: BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: UNION DISTINCT
description: Appends the rows of the second query to those of the first and removes duplicate rows from the combined result.
notes: DISTINCT set operations accept only INT64, BOOL, STRING, BYTES, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC and DATE columns (FLOAT64, TIMESTAMP, DATETIME, TIME and INTERVAL columns are refused); DISTINCT set operations over inputs that can raise an error or are volatile are refused; BY NAME and  CORRESPONDING column matching and the FULL/LEFT/INNER outer set-operation modes are refused (only positional matching is lowered).

name: Array subqueries (in SELECT)
description: An ARRAY expression wrapped around a subquery that returns one column, collecting the subquery's rows into a single array value for each outer row.
notes: An ARRAY subquery with a volatile element (ARRAY(SELECT RAND())) is refused; an aggregate inside a correlated ARRAY source (ARRAY(SELECT SUM(x) FROM UNNEST(a) x)) is refused; a correlated ARRAY source whose WHERE can raise an error is refused; computed NUMERIC elements are refused.

name: EXISTS
description: Returns TRUE if the subquery produces at least one row and FALSE otherwise, regardless of the values the subquery selects.

name: IN
description: Checks whether a value equals any value returned by a subquery that selects a single column, returning TRUE, FALSE or NULL.

name: Scalar subqueries (in SELECT/WHERE)
description: A subquery returning one column and at most one row, used anywhere a single value is expected; no rows gives NULL and more than one row is an error.
notes: A scalar subquery that returns a STRUCT under LIMIT is refused (SELECT (SELECT STRUCT(1) LIMIT 1)).

name: Additional details
description: Further rules for RANGE values, including that arithmetic operators cannot be applied to a range.

name: ARRAY<T>
description: An ordered list of zero or more elements that all share type T; arrays of arrays are not allowed, though an array can hold structs that contain arrays.
