notes: ARRAY<NUMERIC>, ARRAY<BIGNUMERIC> and ARRAY<GEOGRAPHY> columns are refused; a stored ARRAY column is refused under a filter whose predicate can raise (for example WHERE id+1=1) and when UNNEST reads it from a LIMITed subquery.

name: Array type
description: The ARRAY data type, an ordered list of zero or more elements of a single non-array type, which can itself be NULL or empty.

name: BIGNUMERIC
description: A decimal type with exact values, roughly 76 digits of precision and a scale of 38 digits after the decimal point, also named BIGDECIMAL.
notes: An ARRAY<BIGNUMERIC> query result cannot be written to a destination table.

name: BOOL / BOOLEAN
description: Type name and alias for the data type holding TRUE or FALSE; the two spellings BOOL and BOOLEAN are interchangeable.

name: Boolean type
description: Section on the BOOL type: values are TRUE and FALSE, and when sorted a NULL comes first, then FALSE, then TRUE.

name: BYTES
description: Variable-length binary data, such as raw bytes or hashes, that is not interpreted as text and is written with a b prefix on literals.

name: Bytes type
description: Describes the BYTES type: sequences of raw bytes that are not mixed with STRING implicitly, and cast to STRING only when they are valid UTF-8.

name: Collatable data types
description: Types whose comparison and sorting can follow a collation: STRING values, string fields inside a STRUCT and string elements inside an ARRAY.
notes: Only 'und:ci' and '' collations exist; refused by name: collated STRUCT comparisons and casts beyond identity, GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP/CUBE, INTERSECT/EXCEPT DISTINCT, window MIN/MAX/COUNT(DISTINCT), STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG DISTINCT and ORDER BY ... COLLATE syntax over collated values.

name: Comparable data types
description: Types whose values of the same type can be compared with each other; ARRAY, GEOGRAPHY and JSON are excluded, and structs compare field by field in order.

name: Construct a range
description: Creates a RANGE value either with the RANGE constructor function or with a range literal, giving lower and upper bounds of the same type.

name: Construct a range with a constructor
description: Builds a RANGE by calling the RANGE function with a start and an end value, where a NULL bound means that side is unbounded.

name: Construct a range with a literal
description: Writes a RANGE directly as RANGE<T> followed by a quoted pair in brackets, where the lower bound is included and the upper bound excluded.

name: Construct an interval with a datetime part range
description: Builds an INTERVAL from a string of values plus a starting and ending datetime part, such as '2-11' YEAR TO MONTH.

name: Construct an interval with a single datetime part
description: Builds an INTERVAL from an INT64 expression and one datetime part, such as INTERVAL 6 WEEK or INTERVAL -5 DAY.

name: Constructing a struct
description: Creates a STRUCT value using tuple syntax, typeless STRUCT(...) syntax or typed STRUCT<...>(...) syntax.

name: Constructing an array
description: Creates an ARRAY using bracketed array literals, array functions, or generated values such as GENERATE_ARRAY for number or date sequences.

name: Constructing an interval
description: Creates an INTERVAL value from a single datetime part or from a range of parts, using interval literals.

name: Data type list
description: The overview table of BigQuery data types, giving each type's name, a one-line summary, its SQL type name and any aliases.

name: Data type properties
description: Describes behaviors shared by data types: whether values can be NULL, ordered, grouped, compared or collated.

name: Data type sizes
description: Gives the logical size in bytes of each data type, such as 8 for INT64, 2 plus the UTF-8 length for STRING, and 0 for a NULL of any type.

name: Date type
description: A Gregorian calendar date with year, month and day, independent of any time zone, written like 2024-03-15.

name: Datetime type
description: A calendar date and clock time as shown on a watch, down to subseconds, without any time zone.

name: Daylight saving time
description: Rule for civil times around DST changes: a time in the skipped spring hour is read an hour later, and a repeated autumn time is read as its earlier instance.

name: Decimal types
description: Exact fixed-precision numbers, NUMERIC (also DECIMAL) and BIGNUMERIC (also BIGDECIMAL), that represent decimal fractions without rounding error and suit financial work.

name: Declare a range type
description: Declares a RANGE column or variable type by naming the element type in angle brackets: RANGE<DATE>, RANGE<DATETIME> or RANGE<TIMESTAMP>.

name: Declaring a struct type
description: Declares a STRUCT type with angle brackets listing optional field names and types, such as STRUCT<x INT64, y STRING>, and fields may nest.

name: Declaring an array type
description: Declares an ARRAY type by putting the element type in angle brackets, as in ARRAY<INT64>; an array cannot directly contain another array.

name: FLOAT64
description: The 64-bit double-precision floating point type for approximate numbers with fractions, which can also hold NaN and positive or negative infinity.

name: Floating point semantics
description: Rules for NaN and infinity and for approximation: IEEE-754 arithmetic, overflow errors on finite inputs, and sums whose result can depend on order.

name: Floating point type
description: Section on FLOAT64 (double precision) approximate numbers: values are binary approximations, so use NUMERIC when exact decimal results are needed.

name: GEOGRAPHY
description: A set of points, linestrings and polygons on the surface of the Earth, with coordinates as longitude and latitude on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

name: Geography type
description: Section on the GEOGRAPHY type: points, linestrings, polygons and collections of them based on the OGC Simple Features model, with linestring edges following geodesics.

name: Graph element type
description: GRAPH_ELEMENT, the type of a node or edge variable in a property graph query, whose properties can be read by case-insensitive name like struct fields.

name: Graph path type
description: GRAPH_PATH, the type of a path in a property graph, a sequence of nodes interleaved with edges, written GRAPH_PATH<NODE_TYPE, EDGE_TYPE>.

name: Groupable data types
description: Types that can appear after GROUP BY, DISTINCT and PARTITION BY; GEOGRAPHY, JSON and GRAPH_PATH values cannot be used for grouping.

name: Grouping with arrays
description: Two arrays fall in the same group only if they are both NULL, or have the same number of elements and every pair of elements is in the same group.

name: Grouping with floating point types
description: How special float values group: all NaN values group together, 0 and -0 group together, and NULL, negative infinity and positive infinity each form their own group.

name: Grouping with structs
description: Two structs fall in the same group only if they are both NULL, or every pair of corresponding field values is in the same group.

name: INT64
description: The 64-bit signed integer type, holding whole numbers from -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807; INT, SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, TINYINT and BYTEINT are aliases.

name: Integer type
description: Section on whole-number types: in BigQuery the INT64 type, a 64-bit signed integer with no fractional part.

name: INTERVAL
description: A span of time such as 1 year 2 months or 3 days 4 hours, kept as separate year-month, day and time parts, without being tied to a calendar date.
notes: INTERVAL query results cannot be written to a destination table and stored INTERVAL columns cannot be read; INTERVAL values are refused in IF, CASE, COALESCE, IFNULL, NULLIF, IN, IS DISTINCT FROM, LEAST, division, MAX, ANY_VALUE, ARRAY_AGG, COUNT(DISTINCT), array and struct constructors, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, GROUP BY, set operations, window partitions, scalar subqueries, FORMAT and TO_JSON_STRING.

name: Interval-supported date and time parts
description: Date parts such as YEAR, QUARTER, MONTH, WEEK and DAY and time parts such as HOUR, MINUTE and SECOND that can be used to build an INTERVAL, with QUARTER and WEEK converted to months and days.

name: Interval type
description: Section on INTERVAL: a duration with year-month, day and time components in canonical form Y-M D H:M:S, not tied to any point in time.

name: JSON
description: Holds JSON data (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null) as a native value that functions can query by path, rather than as plain text.
notes: IF, CASE, COALESCE and IFNULL over JSON values are refused (no compiler contract).

name: JSON type
description: Section on JSON values: whitespace is not preserved, array order is kept, object member order is not, and the first of any duplicate keys is kept.

name: Leap seconds
description: A timestamp ignores leap seconds: a :60 seconds value is read as :00 of the next minute, and timestamp arithmetic uses Unix-style time that never counts them.

name: Limited comparisons for structs
description: Structs can be compared only for equality or IN, matching fields by position and ignoring field names; less-than and greater-than comparisons are not allowed.

name: Measure type
description: MEASURE, a special type for aggregate calculations that avoid overcounting, evaluated with the AGG function; it cannot be a member of a STRUCT or ARRAY.

name: Nullable data types
description: States that NULL is a valid value for every BigQuery data type, with extra rules for arrays.

name: NULLs and the array type
description: An array can be NULL, but a NULL array is turned into an empty array when it is written to a table or returned as a result, although inside a query the two differ.

name: NUMERIC
description: A decimal type with exact values, 38 digits of precision and 9 digits after the decimal point, also named DECIMAL, suited to financial calculations.
notes: An ARRAY<NUMERIC> query result cannot be written to a destination table.

name: Numeric types
description: The family of number types: INT64 for whole numbers, NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC for exact decimals, and FLOAT64 for approximate values.

name: Orderable data types
description: Types usable in ORDER BY; ARRAY, STRUCT, GEOGRAPHY, JSON and graph element or path values cannot be ordered.

name: Ordering floating points
description: Sort order of floating point values from least to greatest: NULL, NaN, negative infinity, negative numbers, zero (including -0), positive numbers, then positive infinity.

name: Ordering NULLs
description: In ORDER BY, NULL counts as the smallest value, so it comes first in ASC and last in DESC order, unless NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST is stated.

name: Parameterized bytes type
description: Declares a BYTES column or variable with a maximum length L in bytes, written BYTES(L); a longer value causes an out-of-range error.

name: Parameterized data types
description: Type declarations with parameters, like STRING(10) or NUMERIC(10,2), that restrict length or precision for columns and variables; they are not carried through expressions.

name: Parameterized decimal type
description: Declares NUMERIC(P, S) or BIGNUMERIC(P, S) with a precision P and scale S; extra digits past the scale are rounded and values exceeding P digits raise an error.

name: Parameterized string type
description: Declares STRING(L) with a maximum length L; a longer value raises an out-of-range error.

name: Range type
description: A contiguous span between two DATE, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP values, where the lower bound is inclusive, the upper bound is exclusive and either bound may be left open.

name: Specify an offset from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
description: Writes a time zone as a signed hour offset from UTC such as -08:00 or +5:30, directly after the time with no space between them.

name: Specify Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
description: Marks a timestamp as UTC with a Z or z suffix attached directly to the time, or with the Etc/UTC zone name, which is recommended when naming a zone.

name: STRING
description: Variable-length text made of Unicode characters stored as UTF-8; length and substring functions count characters rather than bytes.

name: String type
description: Section on STRING: values must be valid UTF-8 and functions work on characters, with comparison by Unicode code point and no implicit casting to or from BYTES.

name: STRUCT<fields>
description: A container of ordered fields, each with a type and an optional name, and fields may be other structs or arrays; written like STRUCT<name STRING, age INT64>.
notes: A stored STRUCT column is refused under a filter whose predicate can raise (for example WHERE id+1=0) and through a LIMITed CTE (ARRAY/STRUCT relational transport); STRUCT values from a LIMITed subquery or CTE, a scalar subquery with LIMIT or a UNION ALL over such a subquery are refused; STRUCT columns with a GEOGRAPHY field are refused.

name: Struct type
description: Section on STRUCT: an ordered group of typed fields, nullable as a whole, whose named fields are read with dot notation.

name: Time type
description: A time of day such as 13:45:30.5, as read from a clock, independent of date and time zone.

name: Time zone name
description: Names a time zone with an identifier from the IANA tz database, such as America/Los_Angeles, placed after the time with a space between them.

name: Time zones
description: How time zones apply when converting between civil date and time and a timestamp: a zone is a UTC offset or a tz database name, and the stored timestamp itself holds no zone.

name: Timestamp type
description: An absolute point in time, independent of time zone and daylight saving time; it can be displayed in any zone but always means the same instant.

name: Tuple
description: Struct syntax of two or more comma-separated expressions in parentheses, such as (x, x+y), which builds a struct with unnamed fields and is handy for multi-column IN comparisons.

name: Typed struct
description: Builds a struct with an explicit type, STRUCT<field_type, ...>(values); inputs are coerced to the field types and AS aliases are not allowed.

name: Typeless struct
description: Builds a struct from expressions with STRUCT(expr AS name, ...), inferring field types from the values; field names are optional and may repeat.

name: Using array literals
description: Builds an array by listing comma-separated elements in square brackets, such as [1, 2, 3], or from expressions of compatible types.

name: Using generated values
description: Builds an array from a generator function such as GENERATE_ARRAY or GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY, which produces a series from a start, end and step.

name: BETWEEN, IN, NOT IN
description: Filter predicates: BETWEEN checks that a value lies within an inclusive low and high bound, and IN or NOT IN checks whether a value is in a list or subquery result.

name: IS TRUE, IS FALSE
description: Checks whether a boolean expression is exactly TRUE or exactly FALSE, so a NULL input is neither and yields FALSE rather than NULL.

name: Standard comparison operators (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=)
description: Operators that compare two values and return a boolean: equal, not equal, less than, less than or equal, greater than and greater than or equal; comparing with NULL gives NULL.

name: _TABLE_SUFFIX pseudo-column
description: A pseudo-column in wildcard table queries holding the part of each table name matched by the wildcard, which can be filtered to limit which tables are scanned.

name: table_* wildcard tables
description: Queries every table whose name starts with the given prefix in one FROM item, such as events_*, treating the matched tables as a single combined set of rows.

name: Aggregate window functions (SUM, AVG, etc. over windows)
description: Aggregate functions like SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX and COUNT used with OVER, computing a value across a window of related rows while keeping every input row in the result.
notes: ARRAY_AGG ... OVER (...) is refused ("Unqualified numbering function"); CORR and other statistical windows over NUMERIC arguments are refused; STRING_AGG and FLOAT64 MIN/MAX windows whose result depends on tied peers or signed zeros fail with "Non-deterministic order dependency".

name: Navigation: FIRSTVALUE(), LASTVALUE(), NTHVALUE(), LEAD(), LAG()
description: Functions FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE, NTH_VALUE, LEAD and LAG that return a value from another row in the same window, such as the first, last, nth, next or previous row.
notes: A result that depends on the order of tied ORDER BY peers fails with "Non-deterministic order dependency" where BigQuery returns one of the possible values; LEAD/LAG over ARRAY values are refused ("Unqualified numbering function").

name: Numbering: ROWNUMBER(), RANK(), DENSERANK(), NTILE(), PERCENTRANK(), CUMEDIST()
description: Functions ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE, PERCENT_RANK and CUME_DIST that assign each row a position, rank, bucket or relative standing within its ordered partition.
notes: NTILE over tied ORDER BY peers fails with "Non-deterministic order dependency" where BigQuery returns one of the possible results; numbering windows over a source carrying an INTERVAL column are refused.

name: OVER ()
description: An empty window specification that treats the whole result set as a single partition, so a window function is computed over all rows at once.

name: OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...)
description: Window specification that splits rows into partitions with PARTITION BY and orders rows inside each with ORDER BY, so running totals and ranks restart for every partition.

name: Statistical: PERCENTILECONT(), PERCENTILEDISC()
description: Analytic functions PERCENTILE_CONT, which interpolates between values, and PERCENTILE_DISC, which returns an actual value from the data, for a percentile between 0 and 1.

name: Window frames: ROWS BETWEEN ... AND ..., RANGE BETWEEN ... AND ...
description: Frame clause that limits the rows a window function sees around the current row: ROWS counts physical rows before and after it, while RANGE uses a numeric span of the ORDER BY value.
notes: RANGE frames with offset bounds require exactly one INT64 ORDER BY key; FLOAT64, NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC RANGE keys are refused.

name: WINDOW w AS (...)
description: Defines a named window specification once in a WINDOW clause so several OVER clauses can refer to it by name instead of repeating partitioning and ordering.

name: Arrow and Avro serialization formats
description: Lets a read session return rows encoded as Apache Arrow record batches or as Avro blocks, whichever the client prefers.
notes: Arrow buffer compression (LZ4_FRAME, ZSTD), response compression and picosecond timestamp precision options are refused with UNIMPLEMENTED.

name: Column projection (select specific columns)
description: Lets a read session return only the selected columns of a table, so less data is read and transferred.

name: Parallel read streams
description: Splits the data of a read session into several streams that a client or many workers can read at the same time to raise throughput.

name: Row filtering (pushdown filters)
description: Applies a SQL-style row restriction when a read session is created, so only matching rows are returned to the client.

name: Snapshot/timestamp-based reading (time travel)
description: Creates a read session that reads a table as it was at a given snapshot time, so all streams see one consistent view of the data.

name: CreateReadSession
description: Creates a read session for a table, choosing columns, a row filter, a data format and a stream count, and returns the streams to read.

name: ReadRows
description: Reads rows from one read stream in the chosen serialization format, as a server stream of responses, starting at an optional offset.

name: SplitReadStream
description: Splits an existing read stream into two child streams so the remaining rows can be read by more workers.

name: Protocol Buffer or Arrow serialization
description: Appends rows to a write stream as protocol buffer messages or Arrow record batches, together with the schema that describes them.

name: Stream types: COMMITTED, PENDING, BUFFERED
description: Write stream types: COMMITTED rows are visible at once, PENDING rows after a batch commit, and BUFFERED rows after they are flushed.

name: AppendRows
description: Appends rows to a write stream over a bidirectional gRPC stream, optionally at given offsets for exactly-once writes.

name: BatchCommitWriteStreams
description: Atomically commits one or more PENDING write streams of a table so that all their rows become visible together.

name: CreateWriteStream
description: Creates a write stream of a chosen type, COMMITTED, PENDING or BUFFERED, for writing rows into a table.

name: FinalizeWriteStream
description: Marks a write stream as complete so that no more rows can be appended, and returns the number of rows it holds.

name: FlushRows
description: Makes the rows up to a given offset in a BUFFERED write stream visible for reading.

name: GetWriteStream
description: Returns information about a write stream, such as its type, state, target table and schema.
